never conclude "the text was deleted" before looking at the bytes.*

## 2026-09-17 (late) — I TOLD A REVIEWER A FILE HAD BEEN UPDATED; `git diff` SAID OTHERWISE

**Symptom.** In the Tier 1 brief for gate #64 I listed *"`08-MISTAKES.md` entries"* among the changes.
The reviewer ran `git diff -- "PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/08-MISTAKES.md"`, found it **empty**, and blocked.
The file had never been touched.

**Root cause.** The script that was supposed to write those entries did two things: repair a mangled
span, then append to `08-MISTAKES.md`. It **raised an AssertionError on the repair step and exited
before the append** — correctly, since its inputs did not match. I then wrote a SECOND script that
fixed the repair but did not carry the append forward, and described the intended end state from
memory rather than from `git status`. ⇒ **a partial failure of a multi-step script silently became a
partial edit, and my report described the plan instead of the outcome.**

**‼ The same shape as the incident directly above, one level up:** there, a partially-successful shell
command produced a corrupted document; here, a partially-executed script produced a corrupted claim
*about* the documents. Both times the failure announced itself somewhere I was not looking.

**The fix that worked.** Wrote the entries (this one and the one above), and re-derived the file list
from `git status --short` rather than from intent.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULE.** *Before describing a change set — to a reviewer, in a commit message, or in a
handoff — regenerate the file list from `git status --short`. Never from memory, and never from what a
script was SUPPOSED to do: a script that asserts mid-way leaves partial work, and the part it skipped
is invisible in the part it did.*


## 2026-09-18 — I TRUNCATED MY OWN OUTPUT WITH `head` AND ALMOST FILED THE TRUNCATION AS TWO DEFECTS

**Symptom.** Ran `mapfacts.py` for `VICTORY_ROAD_B1F` piped through `| head -25`. It showed 13 objects,
all boulders and rocks, **no trainers**. Our own code says *"B1F carries a trainer … this is how a run
whites out underground"* (`victory_road.py:2345`). I was one step from filing **two** findings: that the
code comment was wrong, and that `get_map_data(...).objects` under-reports map contents.

**Both would have been false.** `mapfacts.py` reports **21** objects for B1F — 8 boulders, 6 rocks,
**5 trainers**, 2 items — matching the decomp's `map.json` exactly. **My `head -25` cut the list at 13.**
The header plus seven warps plus a section title is ~12 lines, so the limit landed mid-list.

**‼ AND MY "CONTROL" APPEARED TO CONFIRM THE FALSE FINDING.** I ran the tool on 1F and B2F, saw named
trainers (Edgar, Hope, Albert…; Vito, Owen, Caroline…), and concluded *"the tool does show trainers, so
B1F genuinely has none."* **That control was invalid**: it tested a DIFFERENT SUBJECT (other maps) and
answered a different question — *"can this tool ever show a trainer?"* (yes) instead of *"did this
invocation show everything on THIS map?"* (no). It was also piped through `head -40`.

**Root cause.** A pipeline limit is part of the instrument, and it is invisible in the result. Truncated
output is not a short list — it is a list of **unknown length** that looks complete.

**What caught it.** The decomp disagreed. I queried `data/maps/VictoryRoad_B1F/map.json` directly
because the finding contradicted something written in our own tree, and the contradiction was worth one
more check before believing myself.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULE.** *Never conclude ABSENCE from output you passed through `head`, `tail`, or any
`head_limit`. Count first — `| grep -c` or `len(...)` — and only then look at a slice. A limit you
applied yourself is still an instrument defect.*
**⭐ SECOND RULE, the one my control got wrong.** *A control on a DIFFERENT SUBJECT cannot establish an
instrument's completeness on THIS subject. To prove a tool reported everything about X, compare X
against an INDEPENDENT SOURCE — not X's neighbours against the same tool.*
**⭐ THIRD, and it is the cheap one.** *When a fresh measurement contradicts something already written
down in the tree, suspect the MEASUREMENT first. Today that instinct was the only thing between a
truncated pipe and two fabricated defect reports.*


## 2026-09-18 — I SPENT A SESSION PRICING A VARIABLE THE DECIDING CODE CANNOT SEE

**Symptom.** I closed the previous day's work by declaring the next step: *"the choice now rests on a
single unmeasured number: the frame cost of one B1F heal round-trip … price it before choosing."* I
then built a 10-agent workflow around that number, and did break-even arithmetic on it myself.

**It was the wrong question.** `estimate_frames_to_level` — the guard whose refusal is the actual
blocker on `#24-levelgap` — has **no heal term and no travel term**. Its whole body is
`ceil(needed_exp / xp_per_battle) * FRAMES_PER_WILD_BATTLE`. The heal round-trip is invisible to it, so
no value of that number moves the refusal by one frame. Under the guard's own model the ground choice
is worth 4.79% against a required 2.05× cut — two orders of magnitude from the decision.

**Root cause.** I had READ that function twice the previous day, for a different purpose (the
calibration question), and both times I was looking at its *numerator*. I never asked what terms it
does not contain. **An absent term is invisible to a reader checking whether the present ones are
right** — the same blind spot as reading a list without counting it.

**What caught it.** A single adversarial recon angle whose only instruction was to attack the FRAMING
rather than the details. It read the function body once and said so. ⇒ the adversarial arm has now
found the decisive answer on three separate questions in this project; it is not a nice-to-have.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULE.** *Before optimising a variable, open the code that makes the decision and check
that the variable APPEARS IN IT. If the deciding function has no term for the quantity, measuring the
quantity cannot change the decision — however carefully it is measured.*
**⭐ SECOND RULE.** *When you set the next session's agenda in a handoff, state WHICH CODE the next
measurement will move. "Price X" without naming the predicate X feeds is how a session optimises a
term that is not in the equation.*

## 2026-09-18 — A CONTROL STOPPED ME FILING A HARD BLOCKER THAT DID NOT EXIST

**Symptom.** Having found that `_exit_training_cave_if_inside()` does not know Victory Road, I inferred
that a B1F grind might be unable to navigate a heal at all — a hard blocker. I wrote a probe to test
it: `calculate_path` from B1F to the Ever Grande Poké Center. **It REFUSED.**

**The control refused too.** I had included 1F→Poké Center as a known-good control, because 278 real
heals from 1F are recorded in prior run logs. It refused identically. ⇒ `calculate_path` is simply not
how cross-map heal navigation is performed — `heal_in_pokemon_center` uses `navigate_to_anywhere`
(`higher_level_actions.py:492`), a warp-chaining graph navigator. **Wrong instrument.** The probe
printed `INCONCLUSIVE` instead of a finding, exactly as designed.

**Why this is worth an entry even though nothing broke.** Without the control I would have filed
"B1F cannot heal" as a measured hard blocker, and it would have killed a ground choice on a false
premise. The B1F heal question remains genuinely OPEN (`#24-cavehealblind`) — which is the honest
state, and a much better outcome than a confident wrong answer.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULE (reinforcing, not new — and that is the point).** *Every probe that can return a
NEGATIVE must carry a control that is known to return POSITIVE. A refusal from an instrument you have
not shown to ever succeed is not evidence of anything.* This is the THIRD time in two days a control
changed the answer, and the SECOND time it prevented a fabricated defect report. ⇒ the rule is not
being under-applied any more; it is now the thing doing the work.


## 2026-09-18 — I TOLD A REVIEWER "DOCUMENTATION ONLY, NO CODE CHANGED". `git status` SHOWED 8 FILES

**Symptom.** The Tier 1 brief for the grind-economics item listed seven documentation files and stated
"documentation only, no code changed". The reviewer ran `git diff --stat`, found an **eighth** file —
`tools/story-dev/probe_live_mapgrid.py`, +27/-7 of real code — and blocked for undisclosed scope. It
also had no changelog or mistakes entry despite fixing three named defects.

**Root cause, and it is NOT that I forgot the fix existed.** I made that fix earlier in the same
session, deliberately and with three fault arms. When I wrote the brief I described **the item** —
the grind economics — rather than **the working tree**. The file list came from what the work was
*about*, not from what was *dirty*.

**‼ THIS IS THE SAME RULE I WROTE THE DAY BEFORE, AFTER THE SAME CLASS OF MISS:** *"Before describing a
change set — to a reviewer, in a commit message, or in a handoff — regenerate the file list from
`git status --short`."* I had the rule, in this file, from yesterday, and did not run the command.

**Why the rule did not fire.** Yesterday's version was filed as the lesson of a *partially-executed
script* — a file I believed changed and had not. Today's case is the mirror: a file that changed and
I did not mention. Same command prevents both; I had indexed it under the wrong failure.

**The fix that worked.** Ran `git status --short`, found the eighth file, documented the probe fix
properly (changelog + this entry), and disclosed it.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULE (STRENGTHENED, because the weak form already failed once).** *Run
`git status --short` and PASTE ITS OUTPUT into the brief or commit message. Not "check" it — paste it.
A rule that asks you to remember to look is a rule you will satisfy from memory; a rule that asks you
to paste output cannot be satisfied without running the command.*


## 2026-09-18 (later) — I VERIFIED THE HAZARD THAT ALARMED ME AND TOOK THE ONE BESIDE IT ON TRUST

**Symptom.** A build recon gave two reasons §Ch23 was the wrong host for a training grind. I verified
the first at source — (a) `DoWhiteOut()` halves money, decomp `src/overworld.c:361`, against a ₽1,741
margin — and wrote BOTH into three files as settled fact. A Tier 1 reviewer blocked: **(b) “the grind
and the basket share one bag” is contradicted by our own code.**

**What the code actually says.** `train_team`'s 118-line body contains **ZERO** bag or item references;
its only healing call is `heal_in_pokemon_center` — a free Poké Center visit. The wild-battle handler
is pure switch logic, and the item-using strategy is trainer-battle-only. **And `Ch24GrindMode._basket()`
— instrumentation written for exactly this question — says in its own comment:** *“THIS IS A READING,
NOT A GUARD … the expectation is FLAT: `train_team` heals at a Poké Center … not from the bag.”*
No evidence file anywhere contains a `basket=` reading showing a drain.

**Root cause, and it is not laziness.** Both claims pointed at the same conclusion — *§Ch23 is the
wrong host* — which I already believed. I verified the one that ALARMED me (money, a hard number with
a decomp citation) and let the adjacent one ride because it agreed. ‼ **The unverified claim was the
one that agreed with me**, which is the direction verification is least likely to travel.

**Why it mattered even though the decision was right.** The reversal stands on hazard (a) alone. But
presenting an unmeasured, code-contradicted mechanism as equally certain is the *“headline carries the
caveat”* failure this project names in SESSION DISCIPLINE rule 2 — and a future agent designing around
“the bag is shared” would have designed around a fiction.

**The fix that worked.** Measured `train_team`'s body myself, found the contradicting comment in our
own harness, and downgraded (b) to THEORETICAL in all three files with the original wording quoted.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULE.** *When two findings support the same conclusion, verifying one does NOT license
the other. Verify the one you find LEAST alarming first — it is the one your agreement will otherwise
carry through unchecked.*
**⭐ SECOND RULE, cheaper and specific to this tree.** *Before writing a mechanism down as fact, grep
for instrumentation that already measures it. `Ch24GrindMode._basket()` existed, stated the expected
answer, and had never been contradicted by a single logged run — one grep would have caught this.*


## 2026-09-18 (later) — THIRD PARTIAL-SCRIPT MISS, AND THE TWO EXISTING RULES COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT

**Symptom.** I reported two fixes to a Tier 1 reviewer. **Neither was in the tree.** It blocked with two
greps: `04-HANDOFF.md` still asserted a retracted claim as flat fact, and the derivation I said I had
added for a 136,135-frame figure returned zero matches anywhere in the diff.

**Mechanism.** One script held three edits. It raised an AssertionError on edit #2's anchor (a curly
quote where the file had a straight one) and **exited before edit #3**. I wrote a second script that
carried forward the two hazard edits and silently dropped the derivation. Separately, my hazard
downgrade covered `03`/`06`/`07` but not `04` — and `04` is the **mandatory cold-start source**, so the
one file a fresh session must trust was left contradicting the three that were fixed.

**‼ WHY MY TWO EXISTING RULES DID NOT FIRE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY.** I already had:
*“regenerate the file list from `git status --short`”* and *“paste its output, do not check it”*. **I did
both.** `git status` showed `04-HANDOFF.md` as modified — from an EARLIER, unrelated edit in the same
session — so the file list said “covered” while the specific edit was absent.
⇒ ⭐⭐ **THE FILE LIST TELLS YOU WHICH FILES CHANGED. IT DOES NOT TELL YOU WHICH EDITS LANDED.** A rule
aimed at the file list is structurally blind to a missing edit inside a file that changed for another
reason — which is exactly the case a long session produces most often.

**The fix that worked.** Applied both missed edits, then **grepped for each intended change and printed
the count against its expectation** before reporting anything. One check fired (the retracted sentence
still matched in `04`); I read the surrounding 330 characters rather than waving it away, and confirmed
it was the *quoted* dead text inside the retraction marker — correct, not a live claim.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULE (replaces nothing; it sits UNDER the two file-list rules).** *After any multi-edit
script, VERIFY EACH EDIT BY ITS OWN GREP and print count-vs-expected. Never infer that an edit landed
from the fact that its file appears in `git status` — in a long session a file is usually already dirty
for some other reason.*
**⭐ SECOND RULE, earned three times now.** *A script that applies N edits must report N results. If it
can exit early, it must be re-run to completion or its remaining edits re-derived from the FILES —
never from the script's intent.*
**⭐ THIRD, mechanical and cheap.** *Anchor strings must be taken from the file, not retyped.* Both
anchor failures this session were curly-vs-straight quotation marks in text I had written myself.


## 2026-09-18 (later) — A CORRECTION CHAIN: AGENT CLAIM → OVER-CORRECTION → NEARLY EDITING A SOUND ITEM

**Four linked errors on one sentence. The chain is the lesson, not any single link.**

**(1) I attached an agent's sentence to my own verification.** I checked `map_data.py` and confirmed
map group 16 contains the Ever Grande Poké Center maps — true. I then wrote *“which §Ch23's leg 10 walks
into to heal”*, which came from an agent, and marked the whole thing **“✅ verified by me”** in FOUR
files. ✅ `heal_at_league` asserts `_on_map(LEAGUE_1F)` (`victory_road.py:2962`) and heals at the League
NURSE on `(16,10)`. *(Tier 1 caught it.)*

**(2) My correction then OVER-REACHED.** I wrote that the Poké Center maps are *“never visited by our
code — exactly two references repo-wide”*. **That was a SYMBOL COUNT, not an occupancy test.**
`PokemonCenter.EvergrandeCity = (EVER_GRANDE_CITY, (27, 48))` is a **DOOR** tile; `heal_in_pokemon_center`
walks through it, so the avatar stands inside `(16,12)` during any Poké-Centre heal. The code never
names that enum member because it detects such maps by **SUBSTRING** — `early_game.py:385`,
`if cur is None or “POKEMON_CENTER” not in enum_name`. My grep found 2 files for the symbol and 7 for
the substring. *(I caught this one, on the next pass.)*

**(3) THE OVER-CORRECTION NEARLY MADE ME EDIT A SOUND OPEN ITEM.** Tier 1 reported that
`#24-egpc-leg4gap` — an OPEN item resting on the bot standing inside that Poké Center — was
contradicted by my note, and declined to make the scope call. **It was my NOTE that was wrong.** The
item's premise is intact and it is left exactly as it was. ‼ Had I “resolved the contradiction” in the
obvious direction I would have damaged a correct item using a bad grep as authority.

**(4) And my “0 live assertions” re-check was UNDER-SCOPED** — it matched one phrasing and missed a
differently-worded restatement in append-only history plus the open item. Tier 1 found both.

**⭐ PREVENTION RULES.**
* *A SYMBOL COUNT IS NOT AN OCCUPANCY TEST.* “Grep finds 2 references” answers “how often is this name
  written”, never “does the program go there”. Ask what the code does, not what it mentions — here it
  matched a SUBSTRING, so the symbol was invisible to the count.
* *WHEN A FRESH CORRECTION CONTRADICTS A STANDING ITEM, SUSPECT THE CORRECTION FIRST.* This is the
  existing “suspect the measurement first” rule, applied to my own retractions — which is exactly where
  I had not been applying it.
* *A RETRACTION'S BLAST RADIUS IS A CONCEPT, NOT A STRING.* Search for the IDEA in every phrasing you
  can think of, including append-only history and open items, and expect to miss one.
* ⚠ *Verifying half a sentence does not verify the sentence.* The map table was mine; the clause about
  leg 10 was an agent's. They were joined by an “and” and shipped under one ✅.


## 2026-09-18 — A GUARD CHECKLIST ENUMERATED NINE OF TEN CALL SITES, AND THE MISSING ONE WAS ALREADY DOCUMENTED FOUR LINES ABOVE

**SYMPTOM.** `probe_ch23_leg_guards.py` shipped, was committed, was cited in `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` and
`07-CHANGELOG.md`, and its headline result — *“on the SEALED map NOT ONE of the nine guards is
True”* — was published as a measurement upgrading a TRACED claim to a READ one. An adversarial
reviewer, given only the diff and told to refute it, read `do_victory_road_chapter` against the
transcription and found **the dispatch has TEN guarded call sites, not nine.**

**ROOT CAUSE — TWO, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT BUGS.**
1. **The enumeration was built by reading the `--- LEG N ---` banners.** The training leg's banner is
   `--- THE TRAINING LEG — BEFORE WALLY, AND IT NAVIGATES ITSELF ---` (`victory_road.py:3387`). It has
   no number, so a banner-driven sweep walks past a real `yield from train_for_victory_road(report)`
   at `:3431`.
2. **Leg 11 is a NESTED call site and only its outer half was transcribed.** The real shape is
   `if _on_map(EG): stock = bag_healing_stock(); if any(stock < qty): yield from ...`
   (`:3462-3467`). The probe recorded `_on_map(EG)` — which merely CONTAINS the call — and I then
   published a “nuance” asserting leg 11 *fires even after the basket is bought, so its self-skip
   lives in the leg body*. **That was false**: the self-skip is the inner `if`, at the call site.

**‼ THE PART THAT MAKES THIS EXPENSIVE, AND IT IS NOT THE MISS.** `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` **already said**
*“‘zero legs fire’ holds post-Wally only; pre-Wally the training leg fires there (its guard at
`:3393` carries no position test)”* — **four lines above the claim it contradicts, in the same
item.** The project knew. The instrument did not encode what the project knew, and the instrument is
what produced the number that got published.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Both instruments corrected to ten call sites and re-run. The sealed-map and
lobby verdicts (**NONE**) survived, but **two control readings changed**: EVER_GRANDE degraded was
published as legs 5/10/11 and is actually **5/10**; basket-bought was 5/11 and is actually **5**. The
false leg-11 nuance is retracted in place with the correction beside it.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **Enumerate call sites by grepping the `yield from`s, never by reading the section banners.** A
  banner is documentation; the call is the code. `grep -c 'yield from' <dispatch>` is the count your
  checklist must match.
- ⛔ **A transcribed guard is the condition under which the call EXECUTES** — for a nested site, the
  conjunction of every enclosing test. An outer `if` is an *input to* the action. (This is
  `CLAUDE.md` §7 “instrument the ACTION”, and it applies to READING code, not only to logging.)
- ⛔ **Before publishing a count, grep the docs for prose about the thing being counted.** A sentence
  in the punch list that qualifies the claim is a spec for the instrument, not a footnote to it.

## 2026-09-18 — THE MOST ALARMING LINE IN A DRIVER FIRED ON A RUN THAT NEVER TOOK THE READING

**SYMPTOM.** The VACUITY arm of `--driver ch24lobby` (pointed at a fixture already inside the League,
so it refuses at the premise) printed:
*“⛔ GRADE: ENTERED_ELITE_FOUR is not False at POST — the guards were talked to, the north doors are
now open FOREVER, and this fixture is NOT the positionally-sealed artifact it was meant to be.”*
**Nothing was talked to.** The run refused before it moved.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `still_untalked = R.get("post_flags", {}).get("ENTERED_ELITE_FOUR") is False`. On the
refusal path `post_flags` is never populated, so `.get()` returns `None`, and `None is False` is
False — which the code read as *“the flag was True”*. **Two states were modelled where there are
three: READ-FALSE, READ-TRUE, and NEVER-READ.** The verdict (FAIL) happened to be right; the
DIAGNOSTIC was simply false, and it is the line a future reader would have believed — it would have
told them a pinned fixture was contaminated and had to be re-minted.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** A three-state read with a sentinel: `….get(name, "UNREAD")`, an explicit
`if _e4 == "UNREAD"` branch saying in terms *“THIS IS NOT A CONTAMINATION REPORT”*, and the alarm
reserved for an actual read-back value, which it now prints.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **`x is False` on a value that may never have been written is a THREE-state test written as
  two.** Use a sentinel default whenever the dict is populated on a path the grade can skip.
- ⭐ **A vacuity arm is not only a test of the grade's premise — it is the only arm that exercises
  every diagnostic on the PARTIAL-STATE path.** Read its full output, not just its verdict. This bug
  was invisible in all three passing arms.


## 2026-09-18 — A PROBE ASKED ONE MAP'S QUESTION OF ANOTHER MAP, AND THE ANSWER LOOKED LIKE A FINDING

**SYMPTOM.** `probe_ch23_lobby_resume.py` v1 ran a CONTINUE check — `calculate_path` from the current
tile to the League lobby's exit landing `(9,11)` — on **every** inside-the-League case. On
`post_hall4_door` (a different map entirely) it printed
`NO PATH — PathFindingError: Could not find a path from (5/3 @ EVER_GRANDE_CITY_HALL4) to (9/11 @ EVER_GRANDE_CITY_HALL4)`.
Read at a glance that says **“the bot is physically stranded in HALL4”** — which would have been a
bigger finding than the one the probe was built for, and it is not true. `(9,11)` is a LOBBY tile; on
HALL4 the question is meaningless.

**ROOT CAUSE.** The CONTINUE target was a module-level constant applied to every case, so the check
silently changed meaning when the subject changed. The probe had ONE target and THREE subjects.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** The target is per-case (`CASES` carries it), and a case with no target prints
`CONTINUE: n/a — no target is defined for this map, and borrowing another map's tile would answer the
wrong question` instead of a scary red herring.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **A check that is valid for one subject is not automatically valid for the next one.** When a
  probe loops over positions/fixtures/maps, every parameter of the check belongs in the CASE row, not
  in a module constant — a constant cannot be wrong loudly, only quietly.
- ⛔ **A `NO PATH` / “not found” / “absent” result is a claim about the QUESTION as much as the
  subject.** Before reporting one as a finding, confirm the question was meaningful for that subject.
  *(This project has paid for the general form of this twice: “never conclude ABSENCE from limited
  output”, and “a control on a different subject proves nothing”.)*

## 2026-09-18 — AN EDIT SCRIPT'S ESCAPES DID NOT MATCH THE FILE, AND ONLY THE ASSERTION SAVED IT

**SYMPTOM.** A patch script written with `\\uXXXX` escapes was pointed at a file whose text contains the
REAL characters (it had been written with a different tool). Every `old` string missed,
`assert s.count(old) == 1` fired with `('cases', 0)`, and the script exited **before writing
anything**. The probe was then re-run and produced output from the UNPATCHED code — which briefly
looked like the fix had failed to work, rather than never having been applied.

**ROOT CAUSE.** Two ways of representing the same text in one codebase: Python `\\u` escapes in
generated patch scripts versus literal UTF-8 in files written directly.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Re-applied with an editor that matches the literal characters, then
**verified each edit by its own grep with an expected count** before re-running.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⭐ **Keep the `assert count == 1` on every scripted replacement.** It is what turned a silent no-op
  into a loud, harmless failure here — the script wrote nothing, so there was no half-applied state.
- ⛔ **After a patch script, re-run the thing under test ONLY once the edits are grep-verified.** A
  re-run over unpatched code produces real-looking output for the old behaviour. *(`08-MISTAKES`
  already records the sibling rule: the file list tells you which FILES changed, not which EDITS
  landed.)*


## 2026-09-18 — A SAFETY GUARD LISTED FIVE FORBIDDEN TILES AND COULD NOT SEE ANY OF THE ONES THAT MATTERED

**SYMPTOM.** `Ch24LobbyMode`'s path assertion was shipped, documented in the punch list, the
changelog, the handoff and the flag registry as *“A PATH ASSERTION IS THE SECOND DEFENCE — the driver
computes the route and refuses to walk it if it contains any of (9,1) (10,1) (9,2) (10,2) (1,7)”*.
It did compute the route. It could not see those tiles.

**ROOT CAUSE.** It built the hazard list as `[tuple(w.coordinates) for w in path]`. A `Waypoint`
carries **its own `map`** and an **`is_warp`** flag, and a step THROUGH a warp records the tile
**ARRIVED AT on the DESTINATION map** — not the tile stepped on. Measured on the real route to the
escalator: the final waypoint is `map=(16,14) coords=(1,6) is_warp=True`, so `(1,7)` — a tile the
guard explicitly enumerates — is simply absent from what it inspects. The same flattening merges
maps, so a coordinate on one map can match a forbidden tile on another.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND.** Not by review, and not by any of the four arms that had passed. It surfaced
during unrelated §0 recon for the League 2F reading: a `calculate_path` to `(1,7)` printed a route
whose last waypoint was `(1,6)` — the wrong tile — and whose second-to-last step would have been a
diagonal, which Gen 3 movement does not allow. **The impossible geometry was the tell.**

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Invert the rule from enumerate-the-bad to assert-the-invariant: **this leg
never changes map**, so any `is_warp` waypoint, or any waypoint off the expected map, is a refusal.
That catches every step-on door on the floor without depending on the enumeration being right.
Plus a **per-run SELF-TEST**: the guard first vets the route to a KNOWN warp and refuses the whole leg
if it reports no hazard. Fault-tested by `POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_BLINDGUARD=1`, which restores v1 exactly
and makes the self-test fire.

**✅ SCOPE, CHECKED BEFORE BEING CLAIMED.** Production story code already handles this
(`sootopolis.py:2143` filters by `tuple(w.map) == floor.value`; `:3340` reads `is_warp`). This was NEW
code regressing against a solved pattern — **not** a repo-wide class defect.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **When a planner returns RICH objects, flattening them to one field is a silent redefinition of
  your question.** `[w.coordinates for w in path]` throws away `map` and `is_warp` — exactly the two
  fields that decide whether a step is dangerous. Ask what each discarded field would have told you.
- ⭐ **PREFER AN INVARIANT TO AN ENUMERATION.** *“never leave this map”* is checkable and complete;
  *“avoid these five tiles”* is only as good as the list AND the reader's ability to see the list's
  members. An enumeration that cannot observe its own members is worse than no guard, because it is
  documented as protection.
- ⭐⭐ **GIVE A SAFETY GUARD A SELF-TEST ON A KNOWN-BAD INPUT, RUN EVERY TIME.** A guard whose only
  evidence is that it never fired has never been shown to work. This one now refuses to run at all if
  it cannot see a hazard it is pointed at.
- ‼ **A fault arm proving the guard's ABSENCE is not the same as proving its COMPETENCE.**
  `POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_NOPATHCHECK` passed cleanly the whole time — it proved the guard was *invoked*,
  never that it could *see* anything. When an arm skips a check, it tests the plumbing, not the check.


## 2026-09-18 — A PATHFINDER ERROR NEARLY BECAME “THE BOT IS TRAPPED ON LEAGUE 2F”

**SYMPTOM.** `--driver ch24lobby2f` reached League 2F, took its readings, then tried to walk home and
raised `PathFindingError: Source (1/6 @ EVER_GRANDE_CITY_POKEMON_LEAGUE_2F) and destination
(3/4 @ EVER_GRANDE_CITY_POKEMON_LEAGUE_1F) are not on connected maps (note that warps don't count.)`.
**My own predictions file, written hours earlier, said in terms that this outcome would mean “2F is a
ONE-WAY POCKET” and would be “a live production hazard”.** 2F is `"allow_escaping": false`, so that
story was entirely plausible.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `calculate_path` plans within **CONNECTED** maps, and **a warp is not a connection** —
the error message says so. The INBOUND leg worked only because both of its endpoints were declared on
the SAME map: `(L1F,(3,4)) -> (L1F,(1,7))`, where `(1,7)` happens to warp, which is why that path's
final waypoint came back already on 2F. Asking for `(L2F,…) -> (L1F,…)` is a **different shape of
question**, and it is the one the planner refuses.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Express the return as per-map segments that STEP ONTO the warp tile: from the
2F resting tile, navigate (same map) onto the delivered tile `(1,6)`; that fires the warp to
`LEAGUE_1F (1,7)`; then navigate (same map) home to `(3,4)`. Measured end to end.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **A pathfinder refusal is a statement about the REQUEST first and the WORLD second.** Read the
  error text before writing the finding: *“not on connected maps (note that warps don't count)”* is a
  description of the planner's contract, not of the map.
- ⭐ **Express cross-map travel as per-map segments onto the warp tile** — which is why production
  uses `_walk_through_warp` plus per-map navigation rather than one long plan. A new leg that invents
  its own long-range plan is re-deriving a solved problem, badly.
- ‼ **A pre-registered falsifier can be WRONG, and grading it honestly means saying so.** P11's
  falsifier named the wrong cause. The prediction discipline is still worth it — it is what made the
  failure legible — but “the run contradicted my prediction” does not automatically mean the world is
  what the prediction said it would be.

## 2026-09-18 — A FIXTURE'S CAPTURE LINE SAID (1,6) AND A RELOAD SAID (2,6)

**SYMPTOM.** `post_league_2f.ss1` was captured with the log line *“✅ CAPTURED … at ((16, 14), (1, 6))”*
and pinned with `(1,6)` written into `FIXTURES.md5`. Reloading it in `probe_ch23_leg_guards.py`
reported **`EVER_GRANDE_CITY_POKEMON_LEAGUE_2F (2, 6)`**.

**ROOT CAUSE.** The capture was taken while the arrival step was still IN FLIGHT. **A save taken
mid-step resumes by COMPLETING that step.** Measured precisely: the tile reads `(1,6)` at frames 0-10
and `(2,6)` from frame 20 onward, stable through frame 600. Both tiles are real and they mean
different things — `(1,6)` is the tile the escalator DELIVERS to (confirming the decomp's reciprocal
warp), `(2,6)` is where the avatar comes to REST.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** The capture now SETTLES first — a bounded loop waiting for the tile to stop
changing — logs BOTH tiles when they differ, and the fixture was re-minted so its documented tile is
its resting tile. ‼ And a second bug fell out of the fix: the RETURN then read the current tile as
the warp tile, stepped onto ordinary floor, and raised a message accusing the game. It now targets the
RECORDED arrival tile.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⭐⭐ **This is exactly what “verify a fixture by RELOAD, never by the capture line” is FOR** — the
  rule already existed in this project and this is the first time it has been observed catching a
  real discrepancy. Do not treat it as ceremony.
- ⛔ **Settle before capturing.** A capture is a claim about a RESTING state; taking it mid-animation
  makes the fixture's documented position a lie that only a reload exposes.
- ‼ **When a fixture records two positions, name which is which.** “Delivered” and “resting” are
  different facts; a row that gives one number invites the reader to assume the other.


## 2026-09-18 — TWO CLAIMS MARKED “VERIFIED” WERE FALSE, AND ONE OF THEM SHAPED A DESIGN ITEM

**SYMPTOM.** While scoping `#24-levelgap` I read two statements that the docs presented as settled,
one of them stamped *(verified 2026-09-17)*, and both turned out to be wrong when I opened the code:

1. *“`train_team` **does not travel** — it grinds the grass it is STANDING IN”* — in the
   `POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_NOWALK` registry row **and** in a `story_harness.py` comment. ✅ Its loop calls
   `_goto_training_area(grass_map, grass_tile)` **every round** (CALL at `early_game.py:2125`; function at `:2049-2068`), ending in
   `_navigate_riding_out(...)`. The claim's SECOND half (no `TRAINING_GRASS` / `best_training_area`
   reference) is true — which is very likely how the false first half survived beside it.
2. *“`team_is_ready(target)` raises terminally”* — in `#24-levelgap` **and** in a sibling research
   note. ✅ `victory_road.py:1847-1912` contains **no `raise` at all**; it returns `(bool, list)` and
   the CALLER raises at `:2138`.

**WHY THEY MATTERED, not just were wrong.** (1) made the `NOWALK` fault arm look like it tested
“the walk is load-bearing” when it cannot — parked off-grass, `train_team` tries to navigate anyway
— so a documented arm was proving something other than its stated property. (2) changes a design
decision: a §Ch24 leg calling `team_is_ready` directly gets `(False, reasons)` back and can **decide**,
rather than inheriting a terminal raise it must work around.

**ROOT CAUSE.** Both were true-sounding summaries of code that was *read once and paraphrased*. A
paraphrase drops the qualifier that makes it false. Neither had an executable check behind it.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Retract at every site with the original text kept beside the correction, and
prefer the SYMBOL over the line number — one of these citations drifted 7 lines within a single day
(`15603 → 15610`) while I was still working on it.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **A “(verified &lt;date&gt;)” stamp is a claim about the PAST, not a guarantee about the present.**
  Re-open the file before building on it. Both of these were stamped and both were wrong.
- ⭐ **When a doc sentence has TWO halves joined by “and”, verify them SEPARATELY.** Here the true half
  lent its credibility to the false one and they had been believed together for a day.
- ‼ **A retraction is not complete until you grep the RESEARCH NOTES too.** I swept `03-PUNCH-LIST`
  and `04-HANDOFF`, declared the retraction done, and a Tier 1 reviewer found the identical stale
  claim alive in a sibling note that the punch list **links to by name** — the second time in one
  session that limiting a sweep to the current-state files let a contradiction survive. **Sweep the
  whole `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/` tree, including `ai-research-notes/`.**


## 2026-09-18 — I BROKE THE “NO BACKTICKS IN A SHELL STRING” RULE THAT I HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN

**SYMPTOM.** Editing `04-HANDOFF.md` through `py -3.12 -c "…"`, bash reported
`syntax error near unexpected token '53'` and `01-VISION-AND-DESIGN.md: command not found` — then
**the edit applied anyway**, with three identifier spans silently deleted from the inserted prose:
`` `#24-trainingbrackets` ``, `` `best_training_area(53)` `` and `` `01-VISION-AND-DESIGN.md` ``.
The result named **no item and no file**, which is worse than a typo: it misdirects a reader to
nothing.

**ROOT CAUSE.** Backticks inside a DOUBLE-quoted shell string are command substitution. The shell ran
the identifiers as commands, took their (empty) output, and passed the remains to Python.

**‼‼ THE PART THAT MATTERS: THIS IS A REPEAT, AND THE RULE WAS ALREADY IN THIS FILE.** The
2026-09-18 entry above it records the same mechanism (it left a literal `0x08` BACKSPACE in a tracked
doc) and states the prevention rule verbatim: *“never put backticks/quotes in a shell-quoted string
carrying prose — write to a file.”* I had written that rule, and then did it again the same day —
which is precisely the failure mode `CLAUDE.md`'s SESSION DISCIPLINE block exists for: *“a rule filed
as ‘the lesson from bug X’ does not fire when you are building Y.”*

**⛔ AND EVERY GATE PASSED OVER THE DAMAGE.** `lint_docs.py`, `audit_doc_consistency.py` and all 56
enforcing gates ran green on the mangled text, because a missing span is still valid markdown and the
control-character gate (#64) only catches control bytes — which this occurrence did not leave.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Repaired from a written .py file, then **proved each restored span by its own
grep with an expected count** rather than trusting the edit.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **Prose containing backticks NEVER goes through `bash -c` / `py -c`.** Write a `.py` file with
  the Write tool and run it. This is now the second recorded instance; treat the rule as absolute.
- ⭐ **A shell error message followed by a “success” line is a CORRUPTION signal, not a warning.** Both
  occurrences printed a bash error and then reported the edit as applied. **If bash complains about a
  string you are writing into a document, re-read the document before moving on.**
- ‼ **Do not let green gates stand in for reading what you wrote.** Nothing in the suite can see a
  silently deleted identifier.


## 2026-09-18 — I FILED A SECOND PUNCH-LIST ENTRY FOR A SLUG THAT ALREADY HAD AN OPEN ONE — AND IT ASKED A DIFFERENT QUESTION

**SYMPTOM.** Closing the cave-heal drive I added `- [x] ✅✅✅ #24-cavehealblind — ANSWERED AND
CLOSED`. `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` **already contained** `- [ ] ⛔⛔ #24-cavehealblind` — still open, 43 lines
earlier, saying *“WHAT REMAINS: prove (by a drive) whether a spin tile **deeper than the exit apron**
can heal at all”*. Two entries, one slug, opposite statuses, the OPEN one first in reading order.
Caught by a Tier 1 reviewer, not by me.

**⛔⛔ AND THE WORSE HALF: THE OLD ENTRY ASKED A DIFFERENT QUESTION, WHICH MY DRIVE DID NOT ANSWER.**
It asks for *“park at a **B1F chamber tile**, force a heal, observe”*. My drive parked on
`TRAIN_SPOT_1F (15,39)` — the EXIT APRON. ‼ Worse still, that entry had **already predicted my
result**: *“HEALING FROM VICTORY ROAD WORKS TODAY ONLY BECAUSE `TRAIN_SPOT_1F (15,39)` **IS**
`VR_EXIT_APRON`”*. ⇒ I ran a drive that confirmed a prediction the item had written down, and then
closed the item as though I had answered its open question.

**ROOT CAUSE.** I filed a NEW item from the name of a question I had in my head, instead of grepping
the slug I was about to use. The project's rule exists verbatim — `CLAUDE.md` P5: *“on finishing an
item, `grep` the tree for its own slug and re-read EVERY hit”* — and I applied it to RETRACTIONS
earlier the same day while skipping it for a NEW FILING.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Merge into ONE entry that states plainly: what was measured (the apron heal,
including PP), what was NOT (any tile deeper), and why the unanswered half no longer blocks (USER
RULING 2 took B1F off the table ⇒ **moot, not solved**). Status `[~]`, not `[x]`.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **GREP THE SLUG BEFORE FILING, NOT ONLY BEFORE CLOSING.** The P5 rule is written for finishing an
  item; the duplicate-creation direction is the same failure and is not covered by its wording.
  **If a slug already exists, you are EDITING, never adding.**
- ⛔ **WHEN A DRIVE “CONFIRMS” AN ITEM, CHECK WHETHER THE ITEM ALREADY PREDICTED IT.** An item that
  states the outcome and then asks for a HARDER experiment has not been answered by the easy one.
  ‼ Read the item's own **WHAT REMAINS** clause and match it to what the drive actually did.
- ⭐ **“MOOT” AND “SOLVED” ARE DIFFERENT CLOSURES.** A question retired by a ruling should say so, so
  that reversing the ruling brings the question back with it rather than leaving a false “answered”.

## 2026-09-18 — A READING WAS TRUE, THEN STOPPED BEING TRUE BEFORE I LOOKED AT IT

**SYMPTOM.** `--driver ch24caveheal` recorded `missing=['C-ATPC']` — *“did not reach the Poké
Center”* — while the route trace printed one line above plainly contained
`EVER_GRANDE_CITY_POKEMON_CENTER_1F`. The grade contradicted the evidence in its own log.

**ROOT CAUSE.** I read the position AFTER the heal generator returned: `at_pc = _here_map() ==
PC1F.value`. But `heal_in_pokemon_center` **enters, heals and walks back out** — so by the time it
returns, the bot is outdoors *by design*. The predicate was correct; the MOMENT was wrong.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Take it from the route the sampler was already recording:
`at_pc = tuple(PC1F.value) in route`. The correct value had been in the run the whole time.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **A STATE READING MUST BE TAKEN WHILE THE STATE HOLDS.** This project already says *“record a
  reading AT ITS TAKE POINT”* for `_take(report, …)`; the same applies to any `if <state>` in a grade.
  **Ask: can this be true and then stop being true before the grade runs?** For anything a helper
  enters and leaves — a building, a menu, a battle — the answer is yes.
- ⭐ **WHEN A GRADE CONTRADICTS ITS OWN LOG, SUSPECT THE GRADE.** The trace was right and the verdict
  was wrong, and the trace was two lines away.


## 2026-09-18 — I CONCLUDED “NO COMMITTED ARTIFACT EXISTS” FROM A SEARCH OF ONE DIRECTORY

**SYMPTOM.** To justify a new probe I wrote, in its docstring, that the only evidence the Victory
Road grind tile rolls encounters was a source comment *"citing a driver reading with **no committed
artifact**"*. An audit agent produced the artifact: `tools/story-dev/ch23route_R15.log:110`, which
reads `[ch23route]     (15, 39) tile_type='Cave' elev=3 collision=0`. I confirmed it exists.

**ROOT CAUSE.** I searched `tools/story-dev/evidence/*.txt` — the directory where drive evidence is
*supposed* to live — found nothing, and reported the absence as a fact about the repository rather
than a fact about my glob. The log sits at the `tools/story-dev/` root, one level up, because it was
written by `--log`, not copied into `evidence/`.

**⚠ WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A WRONG SENTENCE.** The false claim was the probe's stated REASON FOR
EXISTING. Had it stood, a future reader would have believed an unrecorded measurement was being
recorded for the first time — and would have had no reason to go looking for the earlier reading,
which is the one that would have *corroborated* or *contradicted* mine.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Cite the log, and re-justify the probe on a claim that is actually true and
narrower: the old log has **no separating control** — it cannot show the reading is about THIS tile
rather than the map in general. The probe supplies that control (`(15,40)` South Arrow Warp,
`(15,41)` Normal/collision=1, both `has_encounters=False`) and is re-runnable.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **AN ABSENCE CLAIM REQUIRES A SEARCH OF THE WHOLE TREE, NOT OF THE CANONICAL LOCATION.**
  Before writing "there is no X", run the search **unscoped** (`grep -rn` from the repo root, or
  `find . -name`). A glob that returns nothing proves only that the glob was wrong about where to
  look. *This project stores drive output in two places — `--log` writes to the tool root and only a
  deliberate copy lands in `evidence/` — so "not in `evidence/`" is never "not committed".*
- ⭐ **A JUSTIFICATION IS A CLAIM AND CARRIES THE SAME BURDEN AS A RESULT.** I verify findings at
  FILE:LINE and did not apply that standard to the sentence explaining why the work was needed.
  **The "why this exists" paragraph is load-bearing text** — a future reader acts on it.
- ⭐ **WHEN PRIOR EVIDENCE TURNS UP, DO NOT DELETE THE NEW WORK — RE-JUSTIFY IT HONESTLY OR DROP
  IT.** Ask what the new instrument adds that the old one lacks. If the answer is "nothing", say so.


## 2026-09-18 — I LABELLED AN AGENT'S CLAIM “NOT VERIFIED BY ME” AND THEN WROTE IT INTO FOUR DOCUMENTS AS LOAD-BEARING INSTRUCTION

**SYMPTOM.** A 7-agent audit returned NO-GO on a proposed production change. I verified its central
mechanism at FILE:LINE and it held. I did **not** verify its secondary argument — that the
underlying bug was an *"accidental safety net"*, so fixing it alone would expose Victory Road to
`_training_area_allowed` / `_counter_area_allowed` *"for any L35+ party at any story point"*. I
marked it `⚠ NOT VERIFIED BY ME` in the research note — **and then wrote it as a directive into the
punch list, the handoff, the changelog and the decisions log**, in the imperative: *"⛔ Neither edit
is safe without the other"*, *"DO NOT ‘JUST FIX IT’"*, *"the only safe order is … in ONE change"*.
A later check at source refuted it **twice over**.

**WHY IT WAS FALSE.** (1) With no Victory Road row in `TRAINING_GRASS`, `best_training_area` cannot
return Victory Road at all — so a capability fix alone exposes *nothing*. (2) The capability does
not resolve to True: `reachable_maps` defaults every cap to `None`, so `_resolve_caps` would call
`_live_capability("Waterfall", badges)`, which requires a party mōn that knows Waterfall **and**
`BADGE08_GET`. ✅ And the real hazard was the mirror image, sitting unexamined: `best_training_area`
under the production default `allow=None` does **no reachability check whatsoever** — it only skips
areas that HAVE an `AREA_PREREQ` — so it is the **data row without its prereq row** that is
inseparable, not the capability.

**⛔ ROOT CAUSE — AND IT IS NOT “I TRUSTED AN AGENT”.** I applied the project's verification rule to
the claim that *blocked* work and skipped it for the claim that *shaped* work. The NO-GO was the
headline, so it got checked at source; the ordering argument merely told the next session what to
do, so it got a caveat label instead. ‼ **The caveat then travelled with the claim into documents
where it read as instruction, while the label stayed behind in the research note.**

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Verify the secondary claim the same way as the headline — read
`best_training_area`, `reachable_maps` and `_live_capability` — then correct every copy **before the
commit**, preserving the refuted claim inside the text so the next reader sees it was considered and
killed rather than never noticed.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **AN UNVERIFIED CLAIM MAY NOT BE WRITTEN IN THE IMPERATIVE.** If it says DO NOT, MUST, or
  ONLY SAFE ORDER, it is load-bearing and needs a FILE:LINE check — regardless of the caveat next to
  it. **“⚠ not verified by me” is a licence to leave a claim OUT of the instructions, not a licence
  to put it IN with a disclaimer.** A future agent obeys the sentence and never reads the label.
- ⛔ **VERIFY THE CLAIM THAT SHAPES THE NEXT ACTION, NOT ONLY THE ONE THAT BLOCKS THIS ONE.** A
  NO-GO's *reason* gets scrutiny because it stops work; its *recommended ordering* silently becomes
  the plan. The ordering deserves equal proof.
- ⭐ **WHEN AN AUDIT SAYS “X IS AN ACCIDENTAL SAFETY NET”, ASK WHAT X ACTUALLY GUARDS TODAY.** Here
  it guarded nothing, because the thing it would have gated **did not exist in the table**. A safety
  net over an empty stage is not a safety net.
- ⭐ **A COUPLING CLAIM HAS A DIRECTION, AND THE WRONG DIRECTION IS WORSE THAN NO CLAIM.** “A and B
  must land together” sent the next session to do the hard thing first; the true constraint bound a
  different pair entirely.


## 2026-09-18 — MY CONTROL WAS GATED BY THE VERY EDGE UNDER TEST, SO A WORKING RUN REPORTED ITSELF VOID

**SYMPTOM.** `probe_waterfall_capability.py` exists to show that `is_map_reachable` wrongly refuses
VICTORY_ROAD_1F. Because `is_map_reachable` is fail-safe (it swallows errors and returns False), a
bare `False` proves nothing — so the probe carries a control: *"something must come back True, or
the module is simply broken."* I chose `is_map_reachable(EVER_GRANDE_CITY)`. On the third fixture,
which stands INSIDE Victory Road, the control returned **False** and the probe printed
**"EVERY TARGET READING IN THIS RUN IS VOID"** — over a run that had worked perfectly and had in
fact just captured the most valuable reading of the session.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `_gate_key` (`region_reach.py:158-159`) is symmetric, so the Waterfall gate seals
EVER_GRANDE_CITY ↔ VICTORY_ROAD_1F in **both** directions. From inside the cave, my control target
was behind the exact edge the probe was testing. ⇒ **the control was inside the blast radius**, so
it could only agree with the subject, never check it.

**⭐ AND THE “FAILURE” WAS THE BEST RESULT IN THE RUN.** Read properly, that False is the OUTBOUND
seal measured for the first time — a grind at `TRAIN_SPOT_1F` is told the map holding its Poké
Center is unreachable. Had I trusted the verdict line and “fixed the probe”, I would have deleted
the finding.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Make the control geography-independent: `reachable_maps()` returns the
origin at distance 0 and `{}` on error, so **"more than one map came back"** proves the graph built
and traversed at least one edge without assuming anything about what is reachable from where. It
then passed on all three fixtures — and printing the SIZE of that set produced the headline number
(306 maps from Ever Grande, **3** from the grind tile).

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **A CONTROL MUST BE IMMUNE TO THE THING UNDER TEST.** Before accepting one, ask: *"if my
  hypothesis is TRUE, can this control still pass?"* If the answer is no, it is not a control — it
  is a second copy of the experiment. ‼ Here the hypothesis was *"this edge is sealed"* and the
  control sat on the far side of that edge.
- ⛔ **A CONTROL THAT NAMES A SPECIFIC PLACE INHERITS THAT PLACE'S GEOGRAPHY.** Prefer a
  STRUCTURAL liveness check (*did the instrument produce a non-trivial result at all?*) over
  *"X must be reachable"*, which quietly encodes a guess about the map.
- ⭐ **WHEN A CONTROL FAILS, READ THE SUBJECT'S OUTPUT BEFORE BELIEVING THE VERDICT.** This project
  already says *"read the failing line before touching the thing under test"*; it applies to a
  probe's own self-invalidation line too. **A loud VOID banner is a claim, and it can be wrong.**
- ⭐ **PRINT THE SIZE OF A SET YOU TREAT AS A BOOLEAN.** "Reachable / not reachable" hid the real
  finding; `len()` surfaced it in one line.


## 2026-09-18 — I RETRACTED A CLAIM IN THE BODY OF TWO DOCUMENTS AND LEFT BOTH HEADLINES ASSERTING IT

**SYMPTOM.** Having refuted the audit's *"all three parts must land together"* ordering argument, I
wrote the correction into the body of every document that carried it — and a Tier 1 reviewer found
that **two headlines still commanded the refuted version**:
* `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` — item header: *"⇒ WHAT REMAINS: … land that **TOGETHER WITH**
  `#24-trainingbrackets`' `AREA_PREREQ` row — **never alone**"*, three sentences above its own body
  line *"⇒ **this item may be fixed on its own and land first.**"*
* `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` — entry **title**: *"… AND THEN **ONLY IN THE SAME CHANGE**"*, and its
  **THE DECISION** clause *"add both edits and the cap fix as a **single change**"*, directly
  contradicting its own ALTERNATIVES bullet *"✅ NOT rejected — it is safe on its own, and it may
  land first."*

**⛔ WHY THE SECOND ONE IS THE WORSE ONE.** `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` carries a DO-NOT-REOPEN
convention: a future agent is instructed to grep it BEFORE escalating, and to treat what it finds as
settled. ⇒ the one line most likely to be read in isolation, and least likely to be questioned, was
the line still asserting the refuted claim.

**ROOT CAUSE.** I corrected by searching for the refuted *argument text* and replacing each
occurrence. Headlines do not restate the argument — they state its CONCLUSION in different words
(*"never alone"*, *"in the same change"*), so a search for the reasoning does not match them. ‼ This
is P2 (*"the headline carries the caveat"*) firing on a RETRACTION rather than on new content, and I
had written a mistake entry about propagating an unverified claim **in the same edit** that left
these two headlines wrong.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Rewrite both headlines to state the corrected conclusion, and keep a
parenthetical recording what they used to say and why it changed.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **WHEN YOU RETRACT A CLAIM, GREP FOR ITS CONCLUSION, NOT ITS ARGUMENT.** List the phrasings
  the conclusion takes — here *"together"*, *"never alone"*, *"single change"*, *"same change"*,
  *"do not just fix it"* — and search each. **The reasoning lives in the body; the conclusion lives
  in the title, and they share no words.**
- ⛔ **A RETRACTION IS NOT COMPLETE UNTIL THE HEADLINE OF EVERY CARRIER IS RE-READ IN FULL.** Not
  grepped — read. Item headers and entry titles are the halves that get acted on.
- ⭐ **IN AN APPEND-ONLY FILE, THE TITLE IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING LINE IN THE ENTRY**, because the
  file's own convention says its entries are settled. Correct titles there first, not last.

## 2026-09-18 — I HANDED A TIER 1 REVIEWER A SNAPSHOT DIFF AND THEN KEPT EDITING THE FILES IT WAS REVIEWING

**SYMPTOM.** I generated `tier1.diff`, launched the reviewer, and — while it ran — wrote a second
probe plus ~80 further lines into three of the five files under review. The reviewer opened its
report by saying so: two untracked files it had not been told about, `07-CHANGELOG.md` and
`08-MISTAKES.md` each ~37 lines longer than its snapshot, and the very item it was auditing grown by
5 lines. It then had to re-verify its own findings against the live tree to know whether they still
held, and closed with `MISSING_EVIDENCE`.

**⚠ WHAT IT COST, AND WHAT IT DIDN'T.** The three findings survived, because the reviewer noticed
and re-checked. ⇒ the cost was its time and a weakened certification, not a wrong result — **this
is a near miss, not a disaster, and it is logged as one.** A less careful reviewer would have
certified a tree that no longer existed.

**ROOT CAUSE.** I treated the reviewer as a background job to overlap with other work, but Tier 1
certifies **the state about to be committed**. Overlapping edits make that state a moving target, so
the overlap does not save time — it converts a certification into a guess.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **TIER 1 REVIEWS A FROZEN TREE.** From launching the reviewer to reading its report, make no
  edit to any file in its scope. If new work appears mid-review, QUEUE it.
- ⭐ **IF YOU MUST WORK IN PARALLEL, WORK SOMEWHERE ELSE** — run probes, gather measurements, read
  code. Producing *evidence* is safe; producing *text in the reviewed files* is not.
- ⭐ **RE-RUN TIER 1 ON THE REAL DIFF AFTER FIXING ITS FINDINGS**, and check WHERE each fix landed,
  not merely THAT it landed — the same rule Tier 2 already carries.


## 2026-09-18 — I SUMMARISED A 28,000-CHARACTER AUDIT FROM MEMORY BECAUSE MY EXTRACTOR HAD SILENTLY SAVED A PARSE FAILURE INSTEAD

**SYMPTOM.** The research note that exists to preserve a 7-agent audit contained
`⛔ COULD NOT PARSE THE SYNTHESIS` plus 6,000 truncated characters of raw JSON. Everything the
project then recorded about *"what the audit said"* was my paraphrase, with no checkable artifact
behind it. A Tier 1 reviewer flagged it; once the real 27,990-character text was restored, **two of
the audit's own surviving findings turned out never to have been carried forward** — the
`best_training_grass` `allow=None` asymmetry (a THIRD requirement for the change) and
`_MAX_TRAINING_TRAVEL_LEGS = 4` (a claimed second blocker).

**ROOT CAUSE, TWO LAYERS.**
1. My extractor read `spec` at the TOP level of the task output; it is nested under `result`. The
   `try/except` around it fell through to a *"could not parse"* placeholder — **and the script
   printed a success line with a plausible byte count anyway** (9,203 bytes: the header plus the
   truncated dump), so nothing looked wrong.
2. ⛔ **I never re-read the file I had just written.** I went straight from "the script printed a
   byte count" to quoting the audit from what I remembered of it.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Read `result.spec` explicitly, assert it is a string longer than 8,000
characters, and embed it verbatim under a banner marking its refuted ordering advice.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **A FALLBACK THAT WRITES A PLACEHOLDER MUST FAIL LOUDLY, NOT PRODUCE A FILE.** An
  `except:` that substitutes *"could not parse"* and continues converts a hard error into a
  plausible-looking artifact. **If the payload is the point of the file, assert its shape** — here,
  one `assert len(spec) > 8000` would have caught it at the first run.
- ⛔ **WHEN YOU SAVE A SOURCE DOCUMENT IN ORDER TO CITE IT, OPEN THE SAVED COPY BEFORE CITING.** A
  byte count is not a read. ‼ I quoted an audit for hours from a file whose first line said it had
  failed to save that audit.
- ⭐ **PARAPHRASE IS NOT PRESERVATION.** The reason to keep an agent's verbatim output is precisely
  that its *unglamorous* findings — the ones that did not fit my summary's narrative — survive. Both
  omissions here were secondary findings the headline had no room for.


## 2026-09-18 — I STAMPED “DO NOT REOPEN” ON A CLAIM I HAD ARGUED BUT NEVER MEASURED, AND MEASURED IT AN HOUR LATER

**SYMPTOM.** `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` gained an entry ending *"DO NOT REOPEN the question of adding
the row alone, or of fixing the cap alone."* It rested on the claim that fixing `#24-waterfallcap`
alone *"exposes nothing"*, which I had reasoned out from reading `TRAINING_GRASS`. About an hour
later I built the A/B that the project's own rules demand for a *"without X, nothing changes"*
claim — and it printed **"THE SAFE TO LAND ALONE CLAIM IS REFUTED"**, because the fix changes
`_counter_area_allowed`'s answers from inside Victory Road. ‼ I did not go back and correct the
ruling. An adversarial reviewer found the contradiction and noted the stale entry *"is still the
last word in every doc a future reader would grep."*

**ROOT CAUSE.** `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` carries more authority than any other file here: this
project's own rules tell a future agent to grep it BEFORE escalating and to treat what it finds as
settled. I used that authority to freeze an ARGUMENT. **The strength of the marker and the
strength of the evidence were completely unrelated**, and nothing in my process checked that they
matched.

**⚠ WHY THE OUTCOME LOOKS BENIGN AND THE PROCESS IS STILL WRONG.** The ruling's conclusion
survived — the cap fix may still land alone. Only the REASON was wrong. But a future agent would
have inherited *"exposes nothing"* as settled fact and had no reason to re-measure, which is
exactly how a wrong premise outlives the evidence that would have killed it.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Withdraw the DO-NOT-REOPEN, state the measured three-part claim in its
place (executor level unchanged / ranking level changed / only from inside the cave), and split the
entry explicitly into **what is settled BECAUSE IT IS MEASURED** and **what may be reopened
freely** — each settled item naming its source.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **“DO NOT REOPEN” REQUIRES EVIDENCE, NEVER AN ARGUMENT.** Before writing it, name the
  artifact: a measurement, an evidence file, a user ruling. **If the support is reasoning, the
  entry gets “REASONED, NOT MEASURED — reopen if you can test it” instead.** A marker that means
  "stop thinking" must be earned by having already done the thinking's expensive half.
- ⛔ **IF A CLAIM IS TESTABLE BY AN ARM YOU HAVE NOT RUN, IT IS NOT SETTLED — IT IS PENDING.**
  I had already written down that *"without X the bug survives"* needs an arm with X removed. The
  same standard applies to *"without X nothing changes"*, which is the same sentence inverted, and
  I did not notice that until the arm refuted me.
- ⭐ **WHEN A MEASUREMENT LANDS, GREP FOR EVERY RULING THAT PREDATES IT.** The A/B and the ruling
  were one hour apart in the same session; the gap that matters is not time but that a new
  measurement never triggered a re-read of what it might overturn. **New evidence is a reason to
  re-read old rulings, not only to write new ones.**
- ⭐ **SPLIT A DECISION ENTRY INTO “MEASURED” AND “REOPENABLE”.** A future reader can then act on
  the first half at full confidence without inheriting the second half's guesses.


## 2026-09-18 — A PROBE THAT MIRRORS A PRODUCTION SIGNATURE BECAME A DEAD ARM THE MOMENT I FIXED PRODUCTION

**SYMPTOM.** `probe_waterfall_fix_ab.py` monkeypatches `_resolve_caps` to simulate the fix. After
the real fix landed, re-running it reported **11 readings changed** and `n_maps 309 -> 0` — which
reads as a catastrophic regression. It was nothing of the sort.

**ROOT CAUSE.** The fix threads a new `can_waterfall=` keyword through the callers. The probe's
stub still had the old five-parameter signature, so every call raised `TypeError` — and
`reachable_maps` **swallows any exception and returns the fail-safe empty set**. ⇒ the arm was
dead, and its death was reported as `0 maps reachable`, i.e. **the loudest possible output for the
least meaningful cause.**

**⚠ WHY IT WAS NEARLY BELIEVED.** It arrived while grading a prediction, in the slot where a real
regression would have appeared. The only reason it was caught is that the predicted outcome was
*"no difference"*, so a huge difference was obviously wrong. **Had the prediction been vaguer, a
swallowed TypeError would have been written up as a finding.**

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Give the stub the new parameter, AND add a guard: if arm B reports zero
reachable maps while arm A reports more, the run declares itself VOID instead of reporting a delta.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **A FAIL-SAFE RETURN VALUE IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REAL MEASUREMENT — TEST FOR IT
  EXPLICITLY.** Any function documented as *"returns `{}`/`set()`/False on any error"* will hand a
  probe a plausible number instead of a traceback. **Assert the result is non-degenerate before
  treating it as data**: `len(x) > 0`, a key present, a control that must be True.
- ⛔ **A STUB THAT MIRRORS A PRODUCTION SIGNATURE IS A SECOND COPY OF THAT SIGNATURE, AND IT ROTS.**
  When changing a signature, grep `tools/story-dev` for stubs and monkeypatches of it in the same
  commit — they are callers too, and nothing type-checks them.
- ⭐ **THIS IS THE THIRD VARIANT OF ONE LESSON TODAY, SO STATE THE GENERAL FORM:** a control behind
  the edge under test, an arm validated by its expected effect, and now an arm validated by a
  fail-safe value. ⇒ **ASK OF EVERY INSTRUMENT: what would it print if it were simply broken? If
  that looks like a result, the instrument is not finished.**


## 2026-09-18 — I RAN THE PROOF, THEN EDITED THE THING IT PROVES, THEN COMMITTED THE PROOF

**SYMPTOM.** Three documents in one diff asserted **"ALL 65 ENFORCING GATES PASS"**. A Tier 1
reviewer ran the suite on that exact tree and got `FAILED: 1 of 69`. The claim was true when I made
it and false when I submitted it.

**ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS PURELY SEQUENCING.** I ran `run_gates.py` → green. THEN I wrote the
documentation of the fix. One of those sentences put a **drift digit into prose**
(`03-PUNCH-LIST.md`: *"sandbox↔custom drift is now **1**"*), which is precisely what
`probe_drift_restatement.py` exists to forbid — a gate whose own docstring records **13 prior
instances**. ⇒ my documentation edit broke a gate that my documentation then claimed was green.

**⚠ THE PART THAT MAKES THIS WORTH AN ENTRY RATHER THAN A SHRUG.** The docs here are INPUTS to the
suite, not just descriptions of it. Six of the gates read `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/`. So "run the gates,
then write the docs" is not a harmless ordering preference — **it guarantees the run did not see
what I am about to commit.** Every previous green run I have quoted after a doc edit had the same
hole; this is the first time one actually caught fire.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Reword the clause to point at `promote.py --check` instead of stating a
digit (the gate's own suggested remedy, and the convention `04-HANDOFF.md`'s STATE row already
follows), then re-run the suite **as the last action before staging**.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **THE GREEN RUN MUST BE THE LAST THING BEFORE `git add`, WITH NO EDIT BETWEEN THEM.** If any
  file changed after the run — including a doc — the run is stale and the claim is unsupported.
  **Order is: edit → Tier 0 → Tier 1 → fix findings → FULL SUITE → stage → commit.**
- ⛔ **NEVER WRITE A MEASURED NUMBER INTO PROSE WHEN A COMMAND PRINTS IT.** Drift counts, gate
  counts, map counts, file counts. Write the COMMAND. This project has a dedicated gate for the
  drift case because it has recurred 13 times; the general rule is the same one.
  ‼‼ **REFINED 2026-09-18, SAME DAY, BECAUSE THE FIRST WORDING WAS WRONG IN A CORNER AND THE GATE
  CAUGHT ME.** I applied it to ALL THREE drift mentions, including `04-HANDOFF.md`'s STATE-table
  row — and `audit_doc_consistency.py` went red with *"the STATE table's `sandbox ↔ custom drift`
  row states a figure with NO currency marker, so `check_drift` cannot grade it."* ⇒ **that row is
  not prose; it is the gate's INPUT.** The gate grades the digit there precisely so it cannot go
  stale unseen. *(It also read my clever “NON-ZERO” as the literal ZERO — a reminder that a grader
  parses text, it does not read intent.)*
  ⇒ **THE CORRECT RULE HAS TWO HALVES:** state the number in the ONE canonical place a gate grades
  it, with its currency marker (`**N as of <date> (LATEST)**`); and everywhere else point at the
  command. **A restated digit is what goes stale — a graded one is what catches staleness.**
  ⭐ Generalise: before removing a number from a doc, ask **whether something CHECKS it there.**
- ⭐ **A CLAIM ABOUT THE TEST SUITE IS ITSELF SUBJECT TO THE TEST SUITE.** "All gates pass" is the
  one sentence that can be falsified by the act of writing it, because the docs are gate INPUTS.
  ⇒ treat it like a timestamp: it is only true for the tree that was actually scanned.

## 2026-09-18 — A GATE WHOSE OWN DOCUMENTED REPRODUCTION CRASHED, BECAUSE THE SUITE MASKED IT

**SYMPTOM.** `probe_caps_resolve_every_gate.py` passed inside `run_gates.py` and **crashed** when
run the way its own docstring instructs (`py -3.12 probe_caps_resolve_every_gate.py`):
`UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character 'ℹ'`. Its fault arm crashed the
same way, so the sentence *"it must FAIL naming `surf`"* was unreproducible as written.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `run_gates.py` forces `PYTHONUTF8=1`/`PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` on its subprocesses
(`run_gates.py:45`), so the suite never exercises a bare Windows console. I had only ever run the
probe with `PYTHONUTF8=1` myself, out of habit — **so both my testing and the suite shared the same
blind spot**, and every sibling gate carries a `sys.stdout.reconfigure` that I had not copied.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Add the `reconfigure` guard, then re-run both the bare invocation and the
fault arm **with no environment override at all** and confirm exit 0 / exit 1 respectively.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **RUN A NEW GATE EXACTLY AS ITS DOCSTRING TELLS THE READER TO RUN IT** — same command, same
  environment, no habitual flags. If you cannot resist adding `PYTHONUTF8=1`, put it in the
  docstring or make the file not need it.
- ⭐ **A HARNESS THAT NORMALISES THE ENVIRONMENT HIDES ENVIRONMENT BUGS FROM EVERY TOOL INSIDE IT.**
  Passing under `run_gates.py` is not evidence a script works standalone, and standalone is how a
  human debugging a red gate will run it — the exact moment it must not crash.


## 2026-09-18 — I COMMISSIONED RESEARCH INTO A QUESTION OUR OWN CODE MARKS "PROVEN — DO NOT RE-SURVEY"

**SYMPTOM.** I dispatched an agent to *"build the LEVEL-BRACKET MAP of wild training grounds in
Pokémon Emerald"*, listing the bands I wanted covered. `modules/story/training_areas.py:27` opens
with **"⛔⛔ THE L28 CEILING IS THE GAME, NOT A GAP IN THIS TABLE. PROVEN 2026-09-10 — DO NOT
RE-SURVEY,"** followed by 35 lines that already enumerate every route land table by max level, name
Mirage Island as a trap, disqualify the Safari Zone, and state the conclusion I was commissioning
someone to find. **I had read that file three times today and never read its header.**

**ROOT CAUSE.** I treated the punch-list item's framing (*"the table tops out at L28, the high-level
grounds are inert data"*) as the statement of the problem, and went looking for data to fill the
gap. The header exists precisely because that framing is a recurring misreading — it says so:
*"That has repeatedly been read as 'the survey is incomplete'… It is not incomplete."* ⇒ **I became
the next instance of the exact misreading the block was written to stop**, and I did it by reading
the DATA in a file and not its DOCUMENTATION.

**⚠ WHY THE OUTCOME WAS STILL GOOD, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS THE PROCESS BEING GOOD.** The agent
cross-checked against two independent sources and matched 38/38 rows, so the block is now
corroborated rather than merely asserted — and it found a genuinely wrong number inside it (Mirage
Island's odds, off by ~42×). That is luck, not method. A re-survey that had merely agreed would have
been pure waste, and one that disagreed on recall alone could have unsettled a proven fact.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **BEFORE COMMISSIONING RESEARCH, READ THE HEADER OF THE FILE THAT HOLDS THE DATA.** This
  project writes its conclusions as block comments above the tables they concern. `CLAUDE.md` rule
  11 already says to grep `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` before escalating; **the same duty applies to
  DO-NOT-RE-SURVEY markers in code**, which are rulings that happen to live in a `.py` file.
- ⛔ **A PUNCH-LIST ITEM'S FRAMING IS A CLAIM, NOT A BRIEF.** `#24-trainingbrackets` said the
  high-level grounds were "inert data, not missing data" — true — and I inferred the fix was to
  activate them. The file said the opposite: relocation cannot work, train in the dungeon you are
  clearing. **Check the item's premise against the code before acting on its conclusion.**
- ⭐ **IF YOU DO RE-SURVEY A PROVEN BLOCK, MAKE IT AN ADVERSARIAL CHECK OF THAT BLOCK, NOT A FRESH
  SURVEY.** Point the agent AT the block and ask it to find errors. Same cost, and the output is
  either corroboration or a correction — both useful — instead of a second opinion nobody can rank.


## 2026-09-18 — I BUILT A PROBE WHOSE DRIVER COULD NOT DO THE THING IT WAS MEASURING, TWICE

**SYMPTOM.** `probe_p7_reach_calls_in_cave.py` was written to answer *"does anything consult
reachability while the bot grinds inside Victory Road?"* by instrumenting the real functions during
a real grind. It ran twice and measured nothing both times:
1. **Wrong fixture.** `grind_stall_ppzero.ss1` is saved MID-BATTLE. `train_team` is an overworld
   entry point ⇒ *"Cutscene did not end after 8000 frames"*.
2. **Wrong driver.** With an overworld fixture the spin hit an encounter in ~425 frames, and a bare
   `next(gen)` loop cannot fight — so the run sat in one unfought battle for ~89,000 frames.

**⛔ AND A THIRD DEFECT INSIDE THE SAME FILE:** the battle counter read `get_battle_state()` and
reported `battles=0` for a run in which `get_game_state()` said BATTLE at every sample. **The
instrument was wrong about the very condition that was blocking it.**

**ROOT CAUSE.** I reached for the cheapest thing that could advance the generator, and never asked
whether it could advance it *through the situations the generator creates*. A training loop's whole
purpose is to start battles; a driver that cannot finish a battle cannot drive a training loop for
more than one encounter. ‼ I also mis-diagnosed attempt 1 out loud — I said the fixture must be fine
"because the cave-heal drive used it successfully", when the real difference was that **the harness
fights battles and my loop did not.**

**⭐ WHAT SAVED IT.** The vacuity gate — *"only report if battles > 0"*. Both runs would otherwise
have printed **"no reachability calls inside Victory Road — P7 CONFIRMED"**, which is precisely the
answer I was hoping for. **A dead arm produces exactly the silence an absence-hypothesis predicts**,
so an absence claim measured by a silent instrument is worth nothing.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **BEFORE WRITING A DRIVER, LIST WHAT THE SUBJECT WILL DO AND CHECK THE DRIVER HANDLES EACH.**
  A grind fights, heals, walks and can white out. `next(gen)` + `run_single_frame()` handles none of
  them. **If the harness already drives this subject, use the harness** — its extra machinery IS the
  requirement, not overhead.
- ⛔ **CHECK A FIXTURE'S GAME STATE BEFORE USING IT, NOT ITS FILENAME.** One line —
  `get_game_state()` / `player_avatar_is_controllable()` — separates an overworld save from a
  mid-battle or mid-menu one. Several fixtures here are saved mid-battle ON PURPOSE.
- ⛔ **A COUNTER IS AN INSTRUMENT AND NEEDS ITS OWN CONTROL.** `battles=0` agreed with my hypothesis
  and was false. Cross-check any counter against a second reading of the same fact (here
  `get_game_state()`), especially when it reports the convenient number.
- ⭐ **WHEN AN ARM FAILS, MAKE THE PROBE NAME THE FAILURE MODE.** It now prints *"SAT IN AN UNFOUGHT
  BATTLE FOR N OF M FRAMES"* and says a harness driver is required. The next person loses minutes,
  not an afternoon — and does not mistake the silence for a result.


## 2026-09-19 — I CLOSED AN ITEM BECAUSE NOTHING CURRENTLY NEEDED IT, WITHOUT ASKING WHETHER SOMETHING SHOULD

**SYMPTOM.** On 2026-09-18 I closed `#24-trainingbrackets` with five reasons and no code change.
Reason (2) was *"the remedy already ships — `victory_road.py:2087-2090` already grinds on that exact
tile."* The next day the user ruled that training must pick a **level-appropriate ground per
trainee**, and I measured that such a selector returns **`None` for every trainee** unless Victory
Road is promoted — because from Ever Grande the 4-hop travel budget refuses every route ground and
Victory Road is the only candidate at 1 hop. **The promotion I refused is a precondition of the
feature the user wants.**

**ROOT CAUSE.** Reasons (1) and (2) were both of the form *"no current caller needs this."* That is
a fact about **today's callers**, not about the requirement. I checked whether the change was
**necessary now** and never asked whether it was **necessary for what this chapter is for** — and
the chapter's own goal (get a party to a fightable state for the Elite Four) plainly implies a
training selector. ‼ The user had even said so earlier — *"maybe we need to map and mark training
areas for pokemon for level brackets"* — and I read that as satisfied by an existing table rather
than as a request for a capability.

**⚠ WHAT WAS STILL RIGHT, so the correction is proportionate.** Reasons (3)-(5) were real and still
constrain the work: the proposed regression gate is self-refuting, the generic path has no heal-map
row / no cave-exit row / no frame cap, and the code carried a dated warning. **The closure's
ANALYSIS was sound; its VERDICT was scoped to the wrong question.** Re-opening costs a day of
re-reading, not a day of undoing — nothing was built on the closure.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔⛔ **"NO CURRENT CALLER" IS NOT "NO REQUIREMENT." ** Before closing an item as unnecessary, state
  what the feature WOULD be for, and check whether the project's own goals imply a caller that does
  not exist yet. **An item can be unreachable today and still be a prerequisite.**
- ⛔ **WHEN A USER RULING CREATED THE ITEM, RE-READ THE RULING BEFORE CLOSING IT** — not the
  punch-list paraphrase of it. Mine said *"map and mark training areas for pokemon for level
  brackets"*, which is a request for a MECHANISM. I closed it by showing a TABLE already existed.
- ⭐ **A CLOSURE WITH FIVE REASONS IS NOT FIVE TIMES SAFER IF THEY SHARE A PREMISE.** Reasons (1)
  and (2) were the same fact twice ("nothing calls it that way today"). Count INDEPENDENT reasons,
  not bullets.


## 2026-09-19 — INSERTING COMMENTS INTO A PRODUCTION FILE SILENTLY INVALIDATED FOUR DOC CITATIONS

**SYMPTOM.** The Victory Road promotion added a 9-line explanatory comment inside
`_training_area_heal_map()` in `story_mode.py`. `audit_doc_citations.py` then failed with four
findings — `_should_catch` cited at `:2002` but spanning `:2011-2110`, `decide_dex_catch` at `:1566`
but spanning `:1575-1702`, across `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` and `04-HANDOFF.md`. **I changed no behaviour
and no documentation, and still broke four documents.**

**ROOT CAUSE.** A line-number citation is a reference into a coordinate system that **every
insertion above it shifts**. I thought carefully about the blast radius of the DATA change and not
at all about the blast radius of the COMMENT, because comments feel inert. They are inert to the
interpreter and not to the docs.

**⭐ AND IT EXPOSED A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING PART.** One stale citation was
`story_mode.py:2002-1442` — a range whose **start is greater than its end**. It had been wrong since
it was written and nothing noticed, because the gate checks whether the START line falls inside the
identifier's span. Moving the function moved that start out, and the nonsense surfaced. ⇒ **a gate
can be silently under-checking a malformed input for months and still be the thing that eventually
catches it.**

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Re-cite each identifier at its real current span, and repair the malformed
range properly (`2011-2110`) rather than bumping its broken start.

**PREVENTION RULES.**
- ⛔ **AFTER INSERTING OR DELETING LINES IN A PRODUCTION FILE, RUN `audit_doc_citations.py` BEFORE
  ASSUMING THE DOCS ARE FINE** — even when the edit is comment-only. Cheapest habit: run Tier 0
  immediately after touching a `.py`, not only after touching a `.md`.
- ⭐ **PREFER CITING AN IDENTIFIER OVER A BARE LINE WHERE THE PROSE ALLOWS.** `_should_catch` is
  stable; `:2002` is not. A citation naming the function AND a line survives being slightly wrong;
  one giving only a line does not.
- ⭐ **WHEN A GATE FAILS ON SOMETHING YOU DID NOT CHANGE, READ IT ANYWAY.** Three findings were my
  line shift; the fourth was an old malformed range my shift merely uncovered. **Fix the one you
  found, not only the ones you caused.**


## 2026-09-19 — I TRIPPED A TRIPWIRE THE CODEBASE HAD LEFT FOR EXACTLY MY CHANGE, AND DID NOT READ IT

**SYMPTOM.** `story_mode.py` carried a dated note: *"`\"double\": True` … is INERT TODAY … but it
becomes a live misjudgement **the moment `TRAINING_GRASS` gains an entry above L28**, which
`#24-maintain` is explicitly waiting on."* My change added `VICTORY_ROAD_1F (36,40)` to
`TRAINING_GRASS` — **firing that tripwire exactly** — and I never looked at it. A Tier 1 reviewer
