⭐ **AND THE THING THAT MADE THIS CHEAP:** the two fixture/framing mistakes recorded above were
fixed FIRST. Had the drive still been running from `post_sidney_door_open.ss1` (17 % HP, 5 fainted),
this same FAIL would have arrived wearing a plausible wrong explanation — *"of course it lost"* —
and a structural defect would have been filed as a party-strength problem.
⇒ **Removing a confound does not just improve a result, it protects the DIAGNOSIS of a failure.**


## 2026-09-24 — ⚠ I UPDATED FIVE PLACES AND MISSED THE SIXTH — AND THE SIXTH WAS THE ONLY ONE A COLD SESSION *RUNS*

**SYMPTOM.** Having driven the other two §Ch24 room pairs, I updated the handoff BANNER, the QUEUE
HEAD, the STATE table row, the PUNCH-LIST item and the CHANGELOG — five halves, all agreeing that
all three pairs are driven and passing. A Tier 1 reviewer **KICKED IT BACK**: the `HOW TO RUN` block
for `--driver ch24room` still read *"Pairs: `sidney` | `phoebe` | `glacia` (⚠ **only `sidney` has
been driven through the PRODUCTION leg**)"*, and it named only ONE fixture, so it was not even
self-sufficient for the two new legs.

**ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE RULE I ALREADY HAD.** `08-MISTAKES`/`CLAUDE.md` already
says *"a checklist protects exactly what it enumerates"* (P5's origin). This instance adds the part
that makes it bite: **the five places I updated were all NARRATIVE — prose asserting a status. The
one I missed was the only OPERATIONAL one — the block a resuming session COPIES COMMANDS FROM.**
Pair checks P1–P5 are, by construction, mostly narrative-to-narrative, so a narrative-only sweep can
satisfy every named pair while leaving the runnable half stale. ⇒ the stale text was not merely
wrong, it was **the wrong text in the highest-consequence position**: a cold session reading it
would have believed two of the three pairs still needed driving and re-done finished work.

**THE FIX.** The block now carries a three-row table (env value ↔ fixture ↔ destination room) and
states plainly that all three are driven, plus the "three independent legs, not one gauntlet"
caution. Re-reviewed afterwards for an off-by-one in the rows, because a MISMATCHED row would be
worse than the original staleness — it would send a session to run a pair that must refuse.

⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: when an item changes what is TRUE, grep for the place that tells someone what
to RUN — and update it FIRST, not last.** A status sentence is read; a command block is executed.
‼ **COROLLARY: after finishing an item, re-read the HOW TO RUN section specifically.** It is not
covered by P1–P5 except indirectly through P3, and P3 is easy to mark PASS on the STATE-table half
alone. *(Cost of learning this: zero — a Tier 1 reviewer caught it before the commit. That is the
tier paying for itself, and the reason it runs BEFORE step 5 rather than after.)*


## 2026-09-24 — ⛔⛔ TWICE IN ONE SESSION I ASSERTED SOMETHING THE PUNCH LIST HAD ALREADY SETTLED

**SYMPTOM, INSTANCE 1 (morning).** A pre-registration file led with *"whether this party can beat an
Elite Four member **has never been driven end to end**"*. Five punch-list items were already `[x]`
DONE, including the CHAMPION.

**SYMPTOM, INSTANCE 2 (evening).** Having driven all three room pairs, I wrote in FIVE places that
*"the sequencer can be a loop over `PAIRS`, not four bespoke branches."* `#24-leg2spec` — **open, in
the punch list, with a STUB MARKER pointing at a 44-flaw refutation document** — says verbatim:
***"THE 'REPEATING UNIT × 5' MODEL IS REFUTED — DO NOT BUILD IT."*** An adversarial review found it
in minutes and then verified the killer fact at source: **`enter_the_league` and `ch24_chapter_done`
have ZERO occurrences in the entire tree**, so the bridge from the lobby door through the Sidney
fight into leg 1's premise does not exist — and its obvious form had been designed and REJECTED the
same day. ⇒ **the loop could not have taken its first swing.**

**ROOT CAUSE — THE SAME ONE BOTH TIMES, AND IT IS NOT "I FORGOT TO READ".** Both claims were
*generalisations drawn from a result I had just produced myself*. A fresh measurement creates a
strong, specific feeling of knowing the area — and that feeling is exactly what suppresses the
cheap check. ‼ The existing rule (`SESSION DISCIPLINE #11`) is phrased for **escalations** —
"grep `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` before escalating" — so it did not fire for a PREDICTION or for a
CELEBRATORY SUMMARY, which is how the same shape got through twice in one day.

**WHAT ACTUALLY CAUGHT IT, BOTH TIMES.** Not me, and not a gate: an **independent agent given an
adversarial brief** ("refute this claim"). Instance 1 was caught by an inventory agent, instance 2
by a reviewer told explicitly to find how the plan BREAKS. ⇒ the value was in the ADVERSARIAL
framing, not in a second opinion — a confirmatory agent would have agreed with me.

⇒ **PREVENTION RULE, GENERALISED FROM #11: before writing a claim of the form "X has never been
done" or "X can now be done", grep `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` AND `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` for X.** The punch
list is the half that was missed here, and it is not in the session-start reading set as a
*searchable* artifact — it gets skimmed once and then written *about* rather than read *from*.
‼ **COROLLARY: a result you just measured is the WORST moment to generalise from**, because the
generalisation inherits the result's credibility without inheriting its evidence. State what you
measured; grep before you state what it MEANS.


## 2026-09-25 — ⚠ I FIXED THE EXACT HALF I HAD JUST BEEN BURNED BY, AND MISSED A DIFFERENT HALF OF THE SAME PAIR

**SYMPTOM.** On the previous item a Tier 1 reviewer kicked back because `HOW TO RUN` was the one
stale half of pair **P3**. I filed the lesson, and on the very next item I **pre-emptively** wrote
the `--driver ch24bridge` recipe into `HOW TO RUN` before the reviewer could look at it. The
reviewer confirmed that half was clean — **and kicked the item back anyway**, because P3's *other*
half, the **STATE table row**, still read *"UPDATED 2026-09-24"* with no mention of the bridge. I
had updated the banner, the queue head, HOW TO RUN, the punch list, the architecture doc and the
changelog. Six places. Not the seventh.

**ROOT CAUSE — AND IT IS NOT "I FORGOT AGAIN".** The fix I applied was **instance-shaped, not
class-shaped**. I learned *"remember HOW TO RUN"* and dutifully remembered HOW TO RUN, which is a
strictly weaker rule than the one that was actually needed: **P3 names TWO artefacts on its left
side — the STATE table AND HOW TO RUN — and a pair with two left-hand halves fails if EITHER is
stale.** Having repaired one, I felt the pair was handled, and that feeling is what stopped the
check. ‼ This is the same shape as the P5 lesson (*"a checklist protects exactly what it
enumerates"*), one level up: **a REMEDY protects exactly what it enumerates too.**

**THE FIX.** The STATE row now carries the bridge, dated 2026-09-25, with the superseded text kept
quoted.

⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: when a pair check kicks you back, re-read the PAIR'S DEFINITION, not just the
half that failed — and fix every artefact it names.** P3's left side is *"STATE table **+** HOW TO
RUN"*; P2's is *"every KI header **and** every section heading"*. A pair with a compound side is
where a one-instance repair reliably leaves a hole.
‼ **AND THE META-LESSON, WHICH IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE:** *having just been burned by X makes you
diligent about X and no more vigilant about its siblings.* Two consecutive items failed the SAME
pair in DIFFERENT halves. ⇒ **the cheap habit is to grep the item's own slug and re-read every hit
before calling docs done** — which is already the P5 rule, and would have caught both.


## 2026-09-25 — ⛔ AN UNQUOTED HEREDOC SILENTLY DELETED EVERY BACKTICKED NAME, AND THE SCRIPT REPORTED SUCCESS

**SYMPTOM.** Re-pointing the handoff's queue head, I ran a Python repair through
`py -3.12 - <<PYEOF` — an **unquoted** heredoc. Bash command-substituted every backtick in the
prose, so the text that landed read:

> *"…A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE MISREAD YOUR FIRST WIN:  emits a CAPITAL "End of built content." …
> a GENUINE COMPLETION read as . ✅ FIXED + **gate #75**  (RED→GREEN shown)…"*

`story_mode.py`, `HANG CONFIRMED` and `repro_content_end_classifier.py` were **deleted**, leaving
grammatical sentences with the nouns missing. ‼ **And the script printed `queue head re-pointed`,
the marker count was right, and the line count was right.** Every check I would normally trust said
success.

**ROOT CAUSE — AND THIS RULE ALREADY EXISTED IN `CLAUDE.md`:** *"⛔ Prose containing backticks must
NEVER go through a shell string (`bash -c`/heredoc) — use the Write tool."* I had followed it all
session for commit messages and then broke it for a doc edit, because the edit *felt* like code
rather than prose. ⇒ **the rule is about the CONTENT, not the intent of the command.** A Python
script is still a shell string when it arrives via `<<EOF`.

**WHAT MADE IT VISIBLE AT ALL** was bash's own noise on stderr — `story_mode.py: command not found`,
`HANG: command not found` — sitting *above* a success message. ⇒ **when a command prints errors AND
then reports success, the success line is not evidence.** (The same shape as the 2026-09-24 stale-log
near-miss: an edit step errored and the next command's output looked fine.)

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Write the repair script to a FILE with the Write tool, then execute the
file — nothing passes through a shell string. That is now the pattern for any scripted doc edit.

⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: if the text being written contains a backtick, it does not go through a
heredoc — not even a Python one.** Write the script to a file, or use Edit/Write directly.
‼ **COROLLARY: a script that reports success is not evidence that it wrote what you meant.** For a
doc edit, *read back the line you changed* — the corruption here was invisible to the line count,
the marker count, and the script's own exit status, and it would have shipped a queue head with the
nouns missing to the next cold start.


## 2026-09-25 — ⛔ I COMMITTED OVER A RED TIER 0 GATE, BECAUSE A SHELL `for` LOOP ATE ITS EXIT STATUS

**SYMPTOM.** I ran the doc gates and the commit in one chained command:
`for g in lint_docs.py …; do printf …; py -3.12 "$g" && echo PASS || echo FAIL; done && git add … && git commit`.
`lint_docs.py` printed **`FAILED — 1 rule violation(s)`** (R6: the new `POKEBOT_CH24TAIL_INSTRUMENT`
flag was not in `29-DISABLED-FEATURES-REGISTRY.md`) — **and the commit went through anyway.**
`CLAUDE.md` is explicit that *"committing docs over a red doc gate is the same offense as
`git add -A`"*.

**ROOT CAUSE — THE GATE RAN, WAS RED, AND COULD NOT STOP ME.** A `for` loop's exit status is the
status of its **last** iteration, and inside it `… && echo PASS || echo FAIL` **swallows** the
failure: `echo` succeeds, so the loop's status is 0 and the `&&` chain proceeds to `git commit`. ⇒ I
had turned a blocking gate into a **printed opinion**. ‼ The output was right there on screen saying
FAILED; I had already moved on to reading the commit hash.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** The loop now sets a `fail=1` flag and prints an explicit
`TIER0_ALL_GREEN=YES/NO` line, and the commit is a SEPARATE command run after reading it.

⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: never put a gate and a commit in the same shell chain.** Run the gates, READ
the aggregate, then commit as its own command. A gate whose failure is absorbed by `|| echo` is
decoration — which is the same class of defect this project already gates against in its own tools
(*"a gate with false positives teaches the reader to bypass it"*; here I built the bypass myself).
‼ **COROLLARY, and it is the second instance TODAY of the same shape:** earlier a corrupted heredoc
printed success while writing broken text. **A success line is not evidence; the thing it claims
succeeded is.** When a command's output contains the word FAILED anywhere, stop and read it before
reading anything below it.


## 2026-09-25 — ⛔⛔ I BUILT TWO SILENT LIES INTO AN INSTRUMENT ON AN IRREVERSIBLE RUN — AND THE RAW DATA SAVED ONE OF THEM

**CONTEXT.** The §Ch24 P2 drive is **irreversible** (it fights the Champion and clears the game), so
a defective instrument costs the whole measurement. Two of its seven sub-probes returned values that
**looked like readings and were not**.

### ⛔ DEFECT 1 — `str()` ON AN `IntEnum`, AND IT INVERTED THE CONCLUSION
`p2a_ever_overworld` came back **False**. `GameState` is an **`IntEnum`**, so
`str(GameState.OVERWORLD)` is `'7'`, and my `"OVERWORLD" in str(state).upper()` test **could never
match any state at all**. The true answer is the opposite: **5,634 frames of OVERWORLD**.
⇒ It did not merely lose a reading, it **inverted the design conclusion** — the answer decides
whether `ch24_chapter_done()` needs one conjunct or several, and False would have licensed a
one-conjunct predicate that fires *mid-tail*.

⭐⭐ **WHAT SAVED IT: THE INSTRUMENT RECORDED A DISTRIBUTION, NOT JUST A VERDICT.** Alongside the
boolean it kept a per-state histogram, so the raw counts still contained the truth (`'7': 5634`) and
the **irreversible drive did not have to be repeated**.
⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: RECORD THE RAW DISTRIBUTION, NOT ONLY THE DERIVED VERDICT.** A derived boolean
is a claim and can be wrong; a distribution is data and can be re-derived. On any run you cannot
cheaply repeat, log the inputs to your conclusion beside the conclusion.
‼ **AND THE NARROW RULE:** `str()` on an `IntEnum` yields the NUMBER. Compare on `.name`, or on the
enum member itself — never on a stringified int.

### ⛔ DEFECT 2 — A PHANTOM VAR NAME, IN THE FILE ALREADY FIXED FOR IT
`p2d_last_talked` came back **-1**, which is what `get_event_var` returns **silently for a name it
does not know** (`memory.py:393-395`). **`LAST_TALKED` is not an event var** — the Emerald table has
256 entries, none containing "TALK". It is a SPECIAL var, `gSpecialVar_LastTalked`.
‼ **`story_harness.py` WAS ALREADY CORRECTED FOR THIS EXACT BUG ON 2026-09-24** (`VAR_RESULT` →
`read_symbol("gSpecialVar_Result")`), and **the project's own gate caught it**:
`audit_flag_names.py` → `PHANTOM NAMES: story_harness.py: var LAST_TALKED`.
⇒ **THE GATE WAS NOT AT FAULT. MY SEQUENCE WAS.** I ran the doc gates and the undefined-names
ratchet after adding the instrument, and not the flag-name audit — so a gate that existed,
worked, and was one command away sat unrun while I spent an irreversible drive.
✅ Recovered **without re-driving**: the value is a premise-time read, so it was re-read **offline**
from the pinned fixtures (`LastTalked = 0` at the door, control `gSpecialVar_Result = 1`).

⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: ADDING AN INSTRUMENT IS A CODE CHANGE, AND IT RUNS THE SAME GATES AS ONE.**
Before spending an expensive or irreversible run, run `audit_flag_names.py` and
`repro_undefined_names.py` — the two that catch *silent* lies, as opposed to crashes. A crash tells
you it is broken; a silent lie tells you a number.
‼ **COROLLARY: BEFORE AN IRREVERSIBLE RUN, ASK WHICH READINGS COULD BE RECOVERED WITHOUT REPEATING
IT.** Both defects here were recoverable — one from a histogram, one from an offline fixture read —
and that was luck plus one good design choice, not a plan. Making it a plan is cheap: prefer
distributions to verdicts, and take premise-time readings where they can also be read offline.


## 2026-09-25 — ⛔ A FRAME BUDGET CAN *NOTICE* A SUSPENSION AFTERWARDS; IT CANNOT *INTERRUPT* ONE

**SYMPTOM.** The champion leg's first passing drive reported
`intro_frames_spent = 36,457` **against a 6,000-frame bound, without refusing**, and
`battle_frames_spent = 0` for a fight that really happened.

**ROOT CAUSE.** The intro loop waits for `battle_started_frame`. A battle pushes `BattleListener`
above the story generator, so for the whole fight **the loop does not run at all**. Therefore:
1. it never reached its own `if elapsed > budget` check — **a budget whose loop does not execute
   cannot fire**; and
2. when it finally resumed, the battle had already *ended*, so the fight's ~33,846 frames were
   absorbed into the INTRO's elapsed count and the fight step measured **zero**.

‼ **THIS IS A SHARPER RULE THAN THE ONE I ALREADY HAD.** The existing lesson was *"bound anything
that can battle in FRAMES, not iterations"* — and frames **were** the right unit here. They still
could not enforce, because enforcement requires the loop to get a turn. ⇒ the two rules are
different and both are needed:
* **FRAMES vs ITERATIONS** decides whether your number is *meaningful*.
* **WHO IS RUNNING** decides whether your bound can *act*.

⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: a span that BRACKETS a battle cannot be measured or enforced from inside the
story generator.** Take its endpoints from the `on_battle_started` / `on_battle_ended` **callbacks**,
which fire regardless of suspension. Keep the loop-elapsed number too — **the gap between wall-clock
and true IS the measurement of how long the generator was starved**, and that is worth having.

‼ **AND THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS MOST HERE:** the **grade was correct** — all ten readings, one
battle, `BattleOutcome.Won`, nothing mis-graded. Only the **attribution** was wrong. ⇒ **a run can
be entirely right and its telemetry still misleading**, so "the run passed" is not evidence that
every number it printed means what its name says.

### ⭐ AND A SECOND, SMALLER ONE — CAUGHT ONLY BECAUSE THE ARITHMETIC COULD GO NEGATIVE

The first fix computed `intro_true = battle_started_frame - cross_end`, but captured `cross_end`
*after* the intro loop returned — i.e. after the clock had already run through the entire battle.
Result: **`intro_true_frames = -34,729`**.
⇒ **A NEGATIVE DURATION IS SELF-EVIDENTLY WRONG, AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS CAUGHT IN SECONDS.** An
unsigned counter, a `max(0, …)`, or an `abs()` would have shipped a plausible small number instead.
⇒ **PREVENTION RULE: do not clamp or absolute-value a derived duration.** Let it go negative and let
it be obviously broken; a quantity that cannot express "impossible" cannot warn you.


## 2026-09-25 — A LATCH THAT IS TRUE BEFORE YOU START: the absolute/relative bug the chain test caught

**SYMPTOM.** The first full-chapter drive won all five fights (`battles=5`, five `BattleOutcome.Won`)
and then failed with *"the post-battle chain did not reach the Hall of Fame within 34362 frames
(bound 10,000)"* — against three standalone drives that had each measured **2,686** frames on that
same loop against that same bound. A 12.8× departure from a deterministic prior measurement.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `fight_the_champion` decided "the fight started" and "the fight ended" by asking
`battle_started_frame is not None` / `battle_ended_frame is not None`. Those are **MODE-level**
latches set by **every** battle. Driven alone, the leg sees exactly one battle and the question is
sound. Driven as the FIFTH leg of a chain, **four battles have already ended before it begins**, so
both latches were already set: S3 and S4 returned immediately and **vacuously**, and S5 began
pressing for the Hall of Fame while Wallace was still being fought.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Baseline the counters at the leg's own start and ask **relative** questions:
`battles > _battles_at_start` for the start, and `battle_ended_frame >= battle_started_frame` for the
end, so a stale end-latch from battle #4 cannot satisfy battle #5. The chain then passed against the
**same** 10,000-frame bound — which is the proof that the bound was never the problem.

**⛔ WHAT I ALMOST DID INSTEAD.** Raise the bound. It would have "worked" — S5 would have kept
pressing A until Wallace's fight finished and then reached the Hall of Fame — and it would have
shipped a leg whose every battle predicate was permanently satisfied before it ran, with a budget
inflated to hide it. The failure would have moved somewhere else, later, and looked unrelated.

**✅✅ PREVENTION RULE — NOW ENFORCED IN CODE (2026-09-25, same day).** `repro_latch_scope.py`
(gate, registered in `run_gates.py`) parses `modules/story/` with AST and FAILS on any
mode-level battle latch tested against `None`. ⭐ Fault-tested: reintroducing the absolute test
FAILS, and a matcher that sees zero latch reads FAILS as BLIND rather than printing green.
⇒ a future leg cannot re-make this mistake quietly.

**THE RULE IT ENFORCES (kept — the gate covers battle latches; the idea is general).**
⛔ **A LATCH THAT SURVIVES ACROSS STAGES MUST BE READ RELATIVE TO A
BASELINE TAKEN AT THE STAGE'S OWN START — never with `is not None`.** If a predicate can be true
*before* the code that is supposed to make it true has run, it is not a predicate, it is a constant.

**SECOND PREVENTION RULE, from the same failure.** ⛔ **MERGE A SUB-STAGE'S REPORT IN A `finally`,
never on the line after the `yield from`.** The grade printed `heal_ready=None`, which reads like a
second defect in the heal; there was none — the exception propagated and the merge line below it
never ran. *A failing stage is exactly when its readings matter most, and that shape discards them.*

**THIRD, ON METHOD — the one worth the most.** ⭐ **PAIRWISE-PROVEN SEAMS DO NOT PROVE A CHAIN.** All
five legs were independently green and every adjacent pair had been driven together; the bug lived
*only* in the five-deep composition, and no amount of re-driving any leg — or any pair — could have
surfaced it. When N stages share mutable mode state, the N-deep run is a DISTINCT test, not a
formality after the pairs pass.

**FOURTH, ON EVIDENCE CAPTURE.** Stopping a harness externally loses the tail of a block-buffered
`.stdout.txt` — and the tail is exactly where the verdict lives (the harness ends in
`set_manual_mode()`, so it never exits and never flushes). ⇒ **run it with `py -3.12 -u`.**
‼ And the honest follow-up: an audit of all **227** committed `.stdout.txt` files found **zero**
others affected, so this was a consequence of how that one run was stopped — *not* the repo-wide
evidence defect I first suspected out loud. **Re-derive the blast radius before naming one.**


## 2026-09-25 — I DESTROYED `04-HANDOFF.md` WITH A NON-ATOMIC WRITE (and a surrogate pair)

**SYMPTOM.** A doc-edit script died with `UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed`, and
`04-HANDOFF.md` — 900 lines, the file a cold session resumes from — was left at **ZERO BYTES**.

**ROOT CAUSE, TWO LAYERS.**
1. **The trigger:** I spelled 📦 in Python source as `"\ud83d\udce6"`. Python does NOT recombine
   those into one astral character — it holds two **lone surrogates**, which UTF-8 cannot encode.
   ⇒ In a Python string literal, an astral character is `\U0001F4E6` (capital-U, 8 hex digits) or
   the literal character. A surrogate pair is a UTF-16 artifact and has no business in source.
2. **The real defect, which is the one that did the damage:** `io.open(path, "w")` **TRUNCATES THE
   FILE THE INSTANT IT IS OPENED**, before a single byte is written. So the encode error — raised
   *during* `.write()` — happened when the original content was **already gone**. A script that
   merely *failed* destroyed a file it never intended to change.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Recovered the blob with `git show HEAD:<path>` (note: `git checkout --` is
correctly blocked here) and re-applied the session's two edits. Then made every doc write **atomic**:

    def write_atomic(path, text):
        data = text.encode("utf-8")   # <- raises HERE, before anything is touched
        tmp = path + ".tmp-write"
        with open(tmp, "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(data)
        os.replace(tmp, path)

**PREVENTION RULE (one line).** ⛔ **NEVER `open(path, "w")` ON A FILE THAT ALREADY HAS CONTENT YOU
CANNOT REGENERATE — encode to bytes first, write a temp file, `os.replace` last.** The window
between "truncate" and "write" is where whole files go to die, and any exception widens it to
forever.

**⚠ AND THE HONEST PART.** This was recoverable **only** because the file was committed. The two
edits I lost were the ones made *this session and not yet committed* — I had to re-apply them from
the script that produced them. ⇒ a second, cheaper rule: **when a doc edit is scripted, keep the
script**; it is the only backup an uncommitted edit has.


## 2026-09-25 — A CONFIG OPTION MADE MY CONSTANT WRONG (caught pre-ship, worth the entry anyway)

**SYMPTOM.** None in production — this never shipped. Writing §Ch24's new egress proof I hardcoded
`HOME_MAP = LITTLEROOT_TOWN_BRENDANS_HOUSE_2F` and `HOME_STAIRS = (7,1)`, and both live drives
passed, because every profile in this repo is `gender: boy`.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `profiles/*/story.yml` documents `gender: "boy" or "girl"` and `story_mode.py`
passes `cfg.gender` straight to `run_intro`. A girl save resumes in `MAYS_HOUSE_2F` — a DIFFERENT
map. The positive map assert would have made `_settled()` never return True, **timing out a run
that had just cleared the game**, at the single most expensive point in the tree.
‼ Two passing drives said nothing about it: the fixture could not exercise the other branch.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Accept both bedrooms, and **derive the egress target from the live map's
warp table** instead of naming a tile. That is the project's existing standing rule — *"a liveness
check must derive its target from the state the run ACTUALLY reached, and must hardcode no
coordinates"* — so no NEW rule was discovered; the rule was simply not applied on the first pass.

**PREVENTION RULE (one line).** ⛔ **BEFORE HARDCODING A MAP, TILE OR SPECIES, GREP THE PROFILE
SCHEMA (`story.yml`) FOR A SETTING THAT CHANGES IT.** A constant is only constant across the
configurations that actually exist — and "every profile in the repo happens to be X" is a fact
about today's fixtures, not about the code.

**⚠ AND THE HONEST TAIL.** I first filed May's `(4,2)` landing as UNVERIFIED, because this repo
carries no heal-location data. A Tier 1 reviewer fetched the decomp, and I repeated the fetch:
`src/data/heal_locations.json` puts BOTH bedrooms at `x:4, y:2`. ⇒ the caveat is closed on the
FACTS; what remains open is only that no girl profile has ever been DRIVEN. Keep those two apart —
"verified by reading the source" and "exercised by a run" are different claims, and collapsing them
is how a reasoned-not-asserted bug gets written up as solved.


## 2026-09-25 — THREE FROM THE §Ch24 DISPATCH, ALL CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED

### (a) I PUT THE DISCRIMINATOR IN THE WRONG PLACE, AND IT PASSED ANYWAY

**SYMPTOM.** To prove `ch24_chapter_done()` needed more than its two flags, I instrumented
`fight_the_champion` to evaluate a flags-only predicate and the gated one at "the moment the flags
flip". The drive passed and reported **no disagreement** — which, read naively, said my extra
conjuncts were decoration.

**ROOT CAUSE.** The probe sat beside `_take(report, "C-CLEARED")`. That is NOT the moment the flags
flip: `_endgame_done` waits for `cleared` **AND** `rebooted`, so the loop — and everything after it —
runs *after* the SoftReset. The probe sampled mid-EWRAM-reload, where RAM is garbage by
construction, and read `flags_only: False` at `at: ((0, 0), (-7, -7))`.

**HOW IT WAS CAUGHT.** ⭐ **The impossible coordinate.** `(-7,-7)` is not a tile. Moving the probe
inside `_endgame_done`, on the frame `seen["cleared"]` first flips, produced the real result:
`flags_only=True, gated=False` in `EVER_GRANDE_CITY_HALL_OF_FAME`.

**PREVENTION RULE.** ⛔ **AN ARM THAT SHOWS "NO DIFFERENCE" MUST FIRST PROVE IT SAMPLED THE RIGHT
INSTANT.** Print the position/time of every probe beside its verdict — a "no difference" result is
indistinguishable from a probe that never reached the condition. *This is the second time in one
session an impossible derived value (a negative duration, then a negative coordinate) exposed a
broken instrument: **print derived values that cannot be**, and never clamp them.*

### (b) MY JUSTIFICATION FOR THE SHORT-CIRCUIT WAS REFUTED BY THE CURRENT TREE

**SYMPTOM.** I designed `_play`'s "skip §Ch24 when already done" branch and justified it as:
*"otherwise `ch23_chapter_done()` goes False (§Ch24 consumes the Elite Four basket) and the dispatch
re-enters §Ch23 to re-buy one."*

**ROOT CAUSE.** That bug was fixed on 2026-09-24 under `#24-markerwinstate`. `ch23_chapter_done()`
already returns True forever once `IS_CHAMPION` is set. I was reasoning from a docstring's
*forward-dependency note* ("when §Ch24 is built it MUST set its own progress marker") rather than
from the code beneath it — the note described a hazard that had since been closed.

**THE FIX.** The short-circuit is still correct, on a **different and verified** premise: nothing
stops `train_for_league()` re-running on a cleared save, and the §Ch24 party carries mon under the
L65 floor (`Zigzagoon L19`, `Castform L36`) ⇒ a finished game would **grind for hours** and then
re-enter a gauntlet it had already won.

**PREVENTION RULE.** ⛔ **A DOCSTRING'S "FORWARD DEPENDENCY" NOTE IS A CLAIM WITH AN EXPIRY DATE —
RE-READ THE CODE UNDER IT BEFORE BUILDING ON IT.** A note saying "when X is built, beware Y" may
have been satisfied by whoever built half of X. ‼ And a correct feature resting on a refuted reason
is still a defect: the next person will "simplify" it away.

### (c) A CONJUNCT THAT COULD ONLY MAKE THE ANSWER WRONG

**SYMPTOM.** `ch24_chapter_done()`'s first cut required `GameState.OVERWORLD`.

**ROOT CAUSE.** I carried it over from the champion leg's `_settled()`, where it belongs (that code
is waiting for a specific settled frame). As a **gate** it has no discriminating power — the
conjunct that separates "cleared" from "mid-Hall-of-Fame" is `not-on-endgame-maps` — and it opens a
false-negative: the post-game bot is in battle constantly (dex hunting), where `GameState` is not
OVERWORLD. A TIER 1 reviewer independently found the same window via `normalize_to_overworld()`'s
silent 3,600-frame timeout on a cold resume.

**‼ AND MY OWN COMMENT DEFENDED IT WITH A FALSEHOOD** — *"FALSE is the safe direction: it re-runs a
leg that self-skips."* `train_for_league` self-skips only when nobody is below the floor; on this
party it GRINDS. The comment contradicted the very feature it sat next to.

**PREVENTION RULE.** ⛔ **BEFORE ADDING A CONJUNCT, NAME THE CASE IT EXCLUDES THAT THE OTHERS DO
NOT — AND NAME THE COST WHEN IT IS WRONG.** A conjunct that excludes nothing new is pure
false-negative surface. ‼ And "this direction is safe" is a CLAIM about what the code does next:
check that the code you would re-enter actually self-skips before calling a failure cheap.


## 2026-09-25 — I ADDED A CONVENIENCE INSIDE A SAFETY, AND THE CONVENIENCE BROKE THE SAFETY

**SYMPTOM.** `[ch24champion] ⛔⛔ COULD NOT RESTORE THE FIXTURE: name 'os' is not defined —
`current_state.ss1` may now hold a CLEARED-GAME state.` A run that clears the game ended without
restoring its fixture.

**ROOT CAUSE, TWO LAYERS.**
1. The trivial one: I wrote `os.environ.get(...)` in a driver whose `run()` does `import os as _os`.
   A NameError.
2. ⛔ **The one that matters: I put that line INSIDE the `try` whose entire job is to RESTORE THE
   FIXTURE after a game-clearing run.** So the NameError did not merely skip my new capture — it
   skipped the restore. A block added for CONVENIENCE (minting a fixture) disabled a SAFETY (not
   leaving a cleared game behind), and it did so on the very first run.

**BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED.** No damage: all seven §Ch24 fixtures verify OK and PINNED,
`git status` shows zero dirty `.ss1`, and the user's own `Nick - Emerald` profiles were last written
in JULY. Only the harness scratch profiles (`repro-ml`, the `--profile` default, and `repro-fresh`)
were touched. ‼ Checking that was not optional — "probably fine" is not a blast radius.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** Correct the name, and give the capture **its own `try/except`** so that no
future error in it can prevent the restore, with a loud non-fatal log line if it fails.

**✅✅ PREVENTION RULE — NOW ENFORCED IN CODE, NOT PROSE (same day).** This is no longer
something a future agent has to remember: **`repro_restore_guard.py`** (gate, registered in
`run_gates.py`) parses `story_harness.py` with **AST** and FAILS if any statement that is not
itself a `try` stands between a guarding `try` and the `load_save_state` restore inside it.
⭐ FAULT-TESTED BOTH WAYS: re-inserting a bare statement before a restore fails and names the
line; blinding the matcher (renaming the restore call) trips a NON-VACUITY arm, because a gate
that finds zero restore sites is BLIND, not passing. Control green, source restored.
⚠ KNOWN, DELIBERATE LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: it checks only inside the restore's OWN
guarding `try`. Statements EARLIER in the enclosing `finally` (19 of them today) could also
strand a restore; they are reported as an INFO count, not failed, because they are almost all
`getattr`/dict writes and failing them would make the gate noisy — and a noisy gate teaches
the reader to bypass it, which is strictly worse than no gate. If one ever DOES strand a
restore, tighten the gate and accept the noise.

**THE RULE IT ENFORCES (kept, because the gate covers one file and the idea is general).**
⛔ **NEVER ADD CODE INSIDE THE `try`/`finally` THAT PROTECTS AN IRREVERSIBLE ACTION — give the
addition its own handler.** A `finally` that restores state is a
safety device; every statement you put in front of the restore is a new way for the restore not to
happen. ‼ Corollary: when a driver's `run()` aliases a stdlib import (`import os as _os`), a
copy-pasted `os.` is a NameError that only fires on the path you added — which is exactly the path
nobody drives twice.


## 2026-09-25 — I COMMITTED OVER A RED SUITE. AGAIN. So it is a hook now.

**SYMPTOM.** `git push` succeeded and the gate output above it read **`FAILED: 1 of 85`**.
`repro_no_silent_except.py` was OVER its scan-root budget (124/123) because a module I had just
written added two exception handlers.

**ROOT CAUSE — and it is NOT "I forgot to check".** The command was:

    grep -aE "ALL [0-9]+ ENFORCING|FAIL" /tmp/gatesD.out | tail -2 && git add ... && git commit ...

The status gating the commit was **grep's**, and grep had **SUCCEEDED — at finding the word
"FAIL"**. The gate's own exit code was consulted by nothing. ‼ And because the read and the commit
shared ONE tool call, the `FAILED: 1 of 85` line did not exist for me to read until the commit had
already happened. **I could not have caught it by being more careful within that call.**

**‼ THIS WAS THE SECOND OCCURRENCE.** The first is already in this file: a `for` loop whose
`&& echo PASS || echo FAIL` swallowed a red Tier 0 and let a docs commit through. The remedy
recorded then was PROSE — *"read the gate result as its own step"* — and prose did not hold, in the
same session that wrote it down. CLAUDE.md §6: *a rule already broken twice is evidence that prose
failed — write the gate instead.*

**THE FIX: `.claude/hooks/block-commit-over-gates.ps1`** — a PreToolUse hook, sibling to the
`git add -A` blocker, registered as a gate via `selftest_commit_over_gates_hook.py`.

**⭐ AND ITS OWN SELF-TEST REFUTED MY FIRST DESIGN ON THE FIRST RUN.** Version 1 was a BLACKLIST:
*"block a `git commit` that shares a command with a gate `.py`."* The self-test's very first case —
the REAL failing command — came back **ALLOW**, because that command runs no gate at all; it greps
a SAVED log. **The hook would have permitted the exact command it was written to prevent.**
⇒ Version 2 inverts it into a **WHITELIST**: a `git commit` may share its command only with `git`,
message-writing (`cat`/`echo`/`printf`/`tee`), `cd`, `true`. Anything else — grep, tail, `py`, a
for-loop — blocks.

**PREVENTION RULE (one line).** ⛔ **A VERIFICATION READ AND A MUTATING ACTION MUST NOT SHARE A TOOL
CALL** — otherwise the output cannot be READ before the action, and the action ends up gated by
whatever exit status happened to be last. ✅ Now ENFORCED, not requested.

**‼ AND THE DEEPER RULE, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT GENERALISES.** ⛔ **A BLACKLIST OF "WAYS TO GET IT
WRONG" IS WRONG THE MOMENT ONE IS MISSED; PREFER A WHITELIST OF WHAT IS ALLOWED.** My blacklist had
to enumerate every way of reading a result — grep, tail, head, cat, sed, awk, a `.out` file,
whatever is invented next. The whitelist asks the opposite, and its list is short and stable.
*This is the same shape as the roamer-outcome bug found hours earlier: an enumeration of three
fatal outcomes missed a fourth, while the PARITY property could not.*
⇒ **Write the PROPERTY, not the enumeration.**


## 2026-09-25 — A BLOCKED COMMAND RUNS **NOTHING** — including the harmless part before it

**SYMPTOM.** Commit `fb4aea94` was pushed with a message consisting solely of a POSTSCRIPT
paragraph. Its subject line reads *"POSTSCRIPT — THE HOOK BLOCKED ITS OWN INTRODUCING COMMIT…"*.
The actual rationale, the file list and the `Co-Authored-By` trailer are all absent.

**ROOT CAUSE.** The first attempt at that commit was one command:

    cat > /tmp/cm14.txt <<'EOF' … EOF ; git add … && git commit -F /tmp/cm14.txt …

and a PreToolUse hook **denied the whole call**. I then reasoned about the block, fixed the hook,
and re-issued the commit with `cat >> /tmp/cm14.txt` — **appending the postscript to a file I
believed already held the message.** It did not: the `cat >` that would have written it was INSIDE
the denied command, so it never ran. `>>` created the file fresh, containing only the postscript.

**‼ THE MENTAL MODEL THAT WAS WRONG.** I treated the denial as *"the commit was refused"* — i.e. as
if the earlier, innocuous parts of the chain had still executed. A denial is **all-or-nothing**:
nothing in the call ran, not the `cd`, not the `cat`, not the heredoc. The block message even says
so implicitly by naming the whole command, and I read it as being about the commit alone.

**THE FIX THAT WORKED.** History is not rewritten here, so the missing rationale is supplied by a
follow-up commit that names `fb4aea94` explicitly. ⇒ the information lives in `07-CHANGELOG.md`
(which already carried the full story) and in that follow-up; only `git log --oneline` is thin, and
it now has a neighbour that explains why.

**PREVENTION RULE (one line).** ⛔ **AFTER A DENIED TOOL CALL, ASSUME NOTHING IN IT HAPPENED — and
re-create side effects with `>` , never `>>`.** An append presumes a predecessor; a denial
guarantees there was none.

**‼ AND THE SECOND-ORDER RULE, which is the more useful one.** ⛔ **BUILD THE COMMIT MESSAGE IN ITS
OWN TOOL CALL, BEFORE THE COMMIT CALL.** Bundling message-authoring with the commit means any
refusal of the commit silently discards the message — and the retry then looks like it has one.
*(This is the same family as the rule that produced the hook in the first place: a READ and an
ACTION, or here an AUTHORING step and an ACTION, must not share a call.)*

## 2026-09-25 (later still) — seven mistakes from driving the PC-first HM path, all in the INSTRUMENT

‼ The subject under test was correct on its first run. **Every defect below was in the test or the
edit tooling** — which is the shape this file keeps recording, and the reason it keeps recording it.

### 1. ⛔ THE ACCEPTANCE BANNER LIED UNDER TWO OF THREE ARMS
**Symptom:** all three arms printed *"a carrier we ALREADY OWN is found in the box and withdrawn"*.
**Root cause:** the claim sentence was arm-independent prose in a single `log()`. Under `nobox`
nothing was injected; under `skipfix` the carrier is deliberately NOT withdrawn — that is the entire
point of the arm.
**Why it matters more than it looks:** grepping the committed evidence for `ACCEPTANCE: PASS` would
have returned three lines all asserting a withdraw, and **the two that did not withdraw are exactly
the two that make the first one mean anything.**
**Fix:** `_claim` is now a per-arm dict; each arm states its own, different claim.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **A VERDICT LINE IS A HEADLINE, AND A FAULT ARM'S HEADLINE IS NOT THE HAPPY
PATH'S.** If a driver has arms, its acceptance sentence must be arm-dependent or it is false for
every arm but one.

### 2. ⛔ AN UNBOUNDED FAULT ARM PRINTED **NO VERDICT AT ALL**
**Symptom:** the first `skipfix` run exited 0 and logged nothing from the driver.
**Root cause:** with the block disarmed the errand does not terminate — it hunts. The harness frame
budget (120,000) expired while the generator was still suspended, so neither the grade nor the
`finally` (and so not the fixture restore) ever ran. Its evidence existed only as a party roster
buried in a 12,000-line log.
**Fix:** `_yield_bounded_by_frames(errand, 30000)`, then grade the NEGATIVE explicitly.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **AN ARM WHOSE EVIDENCE A HUMAN MUST RECONSTRUCT FROM A LOG IS NOT A GRADED
ARM.** A skip-the-fix arm removes the thing that makes the errand terminate — so it must be bounded
by construction, never by the harness budget.
**‼ AND IT HAS A SECOND ROUTE, FOUND BY THE TIER 1 REVIEWER ON THIS SAME ITEM:** having bounded the
INNER loop, I then wrote a handoff recipe printing ONE command at `--frames 30000` while naming
`skipfix` in the same sentence — and that arm prints its verdict at **f30426**, so the copied command
dies on the harness's OUTER cap with no verdict. ⇒ **BOUNDING ONE LOOP AND DOCUMENTING THE OTHER IS
NOT THE SAME AS MAKING THE ARM REPRODUCIBLE.** Every arm gets its OWN complete command; a per-arm
frame ceiling mentioned in parentheses is not a runnable instruction.

### 3. ⛔ `str.replace(old, new, 1)` WITH NO ASSERT — A SILENT NO-OP
**Symptom:** `--driver hmpcfirst` was rejected by argparse: *"invalid choice"*.
**Root cause:** the registration line was `s.replace('"ch24gauntlet",', ...)` but the choices list
ends `"ch24gauntlet"])` — **no trailing comma**. `replace` matched nothing and returned the string
unchanged. Every OTHER edit in that same script asserted its anchor count; this one line did not.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **EVERY ANCHORED EDIT ASSERTS ITS MATCH COUNT — NO EXCEPTIONS, INCLUDING THE
ONE-LINERS.** A patch script without an assert does not fail; it succeeds at doing nothing, and the
failure surfaces somewhere unrelated.

### 4. ⛔ AN ANCHOR THAT MATCHED **83 TIMES**, AIMED AT ONE DRIVER
**Symptom:** fixing mistake 1, the anchor `log(f"[{TAG}] ACCEPTANCE: ` scored **83** — every driver
in `story_harness.py` logs that line. Unscoped, the edit would have rewritten **a different
driver's verdict line**, leaving both wrong and the wrong one silent.
**Also, the attempt before it scored 0** — it quoted a backslash-escaped `\u2014` while the file
holds the real em-dash.
**Fix:** slice the region between `class HmPcFirstMode` and the next top-level `def`, and assert
uniqueness THERE.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **IN A 25,000-LINE FILE OF NEAR-IDENTICAL DRIVERS, SCOPE THE ANCHOR TO ITS
CLASS BEFORE MATCHING, AND ASSERT UNIQUENESS INSIDE THAT SCOPE.** A global-unique assert is what
turned a silent cross-driver corruption into a loud, cheap failure — it is the only reason this is
a note here rather than a defect in another driver.

### 5. ⛔ THE DOCS QUOTED A PID THAT WAS NOT IN THE COMMITTED EVIDENCE
**Symptom:** `07-CHANGELOG.md` and `29-DISABLED-FEATURES-REGISTRY.md` cited
`boxed_hm_learner_pids = ['EA0300DF']` and `['37D27792']`. The committed evidence files hold
`F12C7BDE` and `7DBC0999`. **Zero overlap.**
**Root cause:** the numbers were transcribed from the FIRST runs. Mistake 1 above then forced all
three arms to be re-run, which overwrote the evidence files — and `debug_create_pokemon` rolls a
**fresh random personality value every run**, so every PID changed. The prose was never re-read
against the file it now shipped beside.
**How it was caught:** the story-drive rule *"grep the committed file for the line your claim rests
on"*. It earned its keep on its first application here — a reader grepping the evidence for the
quoted PID would have found nothing and reasonably concluded the claim was invented.
**Fix:** both values corrected, AND the prose now states that the PID is random per run and that
the durable claim is the IDENTITY RELATION, never the literal value.
**‼ AND IT RECURRED THE SAME DAY, WHICH IS WHY THE RULE IS NOT "BE MORE CAREFUL".** Adding `H-CANCONTINUE` forced ANOTHER re-run of every arm, and the corrected pair (`F12C7BDE`/`7DBC0999`) went stale exactly as the first pair had. ⇒ the second fix was not to re-transcribe a third set of values but to **DELETE THE LITERALS** from every live claim and state the RELATION instead. A doc that needs re-editing after every run is a doc that will eventually ship wrong.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔⛔ **RE-RUNNING AN ARM INVALIDATES EVERY NUMBER ALREADY WRITTEN ABOUT IT.**
After any re-run, re-grep the evidence for every literal quoted in the docs. ⭐ And prefer to quote
the RELATION (*"the PID we injected is the one that moved"*) over the VALUE — a value regenerated
by the fixture tooling is not a fact about the system, and writing it as though it were creates a
citation that rots on the next run.

### 6. ⛔⛔ MY OWN "CAN THE BOT CONTINUE" PROOF WAS SATISFIED BY THE DOOR IT HAD JUST WALKED OUT OF
**Symptom:** `H-CANCONTINUE` recorded a PASS having pathed **one waypoint**.
**Root cause:** the errand ends on `(5, 7)`; the live map's warp list begins `(5, 6)` — the Poké
Centre door directly above. The check took the FIRST warp that pathed and broke out of the loop. ⇒
it proved the bot could step back INSIDE the building it had just left, which is the opposite of
egress.
**‼ THE RULE HAD ALREADY WARNED OF THIS, IN THE VERY ADVISORY THAT PROMPTED THE CHECK:** *"Walking
to a DOOR tile ends you INSIDE the building, which skips that check — target the tile in FRONT of
the door."* I read it, added the check, and walked into it anyway.
**Why faithful porting was not enough:** the pattern came from `pokemon_league.py`'s
`C-CANCONTINUE`, where the bot stands in a **BEDROOM whose only warp IS the stairs** — there,
first-warp-that-paths genuinely IS egress. On an open city map with nine warps, one of them under
your feet, it is not.
**Fix:** try EVERY warp (no early break) and require at least one exit at Chebyshev distance > 1.
Measured after: 9 of 9 reachable, 8 non-adjacent, 11–46 waypoints.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔⛔ **A PATTERN CARRIES ITS ORIGINAL MAP'S ASSUMPTIONS WITH IT.** When porting
a proven check, ask what was true of the ORIGINAL situation that made it sufficient — and re-derive
that premise for the new one. ⭐ And for egress specifically: **an exit ADJACENT to where you stand
cannot distinguish "can continue" from "is standing next to a door"** — exclude it, and prefer a
stated property (non-adjacency) over a threshold on waypoint count.

### 7. ⛔ THE SAME PORT DROPPED `reraise_if_aborting` — SO A WHITEOUT WOULD HAVE BEEN MASKED
**Symptom:** none visible. The diff-triggered advisory (`R-EXCEPT`) flagged the new handler on the
commit that introduced it.
**Root cause:** `pokemon_league.py:3445-3449` is
`except Exception as error:` / **`reraise_if_aborting(error)`** / `raise BotModeError(...)`. My port
kept the comment, the shape and the message and dropped **line 3446**. ⇒ a `StoryAbort` raised
during the map read — which is exactly what a whiteout latches — would be converted into a
`BotModeError`, the verdict would blame the map read, and `whiteouts` would stay **0**.
**Also fixed in the same pass:** `_box_pids`'s bare `except Exception: return set()`. That helper
feeds the GRADED identity claim, not just telemetry, so a swallowed abort there becomes a quiet
*"the carrier is not in the box"*.
**‼ THIS IS MISTAKE #6 AGAIN, ONE COMMIT LATER.** #6 was *"a pattern carries its original map's
assumptions with it"*; #7 is the same porting failure in its other form — **a port also LOSES the
lines you did not consciously copy**, and those are precisely the lines that exist because something
once went wrong without them.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔⛔ **PORTING IS NOT TRANSCRIPTION — DIFF THE PORT AGAINST THE ORIGINAL.**
Read the source once and retype it and you will reproduce its *shape* while dropping its *scars*.
Every line in a hardened block is load-bearing; if you cannot say why a line is there, that is the
line to check, not the line to skip.

### ⭐ AND ONE NEAR-MISS THAT COST NOTHING, BECAUSE IT WAS CHECKED OFFLINE FIRST
**Surf was the obvious HM to test with, and it would have made the whole drive VACUOUS** —
Zigzagoon L3 learns Surf, so `hm_learner_slot` returns a party slot and the PC-first block is never
reached, while the run still prints PASS. Caught by resolving the learnsets against
`modules/data/species.json` (Waterfall = move 127) **before spending a frame**.
**Prevention rule:** ⭐ **WHEN A TEST'S VALIDITY RESTS ON A DATA FACT, RESOLVE THAT FACT OFFLINE
AGAINST THE DATA FILE BEFORE RUNNING — and have the driver ASSERT it at runtime as well.** The
offline check is cheap; the runtime assert is what protects the test after the fixture drifts.

## 2026-09-26 — the WRAP-UP's own SEVEN mistakes: the P5 failure verbatim, then its own rule recurring

Context: the session was ending at the user's request. Nothing was in flight; the only work was
recording that the daily upstream check had found the mirror 2 commits behind, and parking the sync.
A Tier 2 cold-start audit returned **FAIL** on that two-file change.

### 1. ⛔⛔ THE FACT LIVED IN THREE PLACES AND I UPDATED TWO — SO THE PAIR CHECK PASSED
**Symptom:** the handoff banner and the `NEXT ACTIONS` queue head both said *"upstream moved to
`84c6064c`, the mirror is 2 commits behind"*. The STATE table's `upstream` row still read
*"checked **2026-09-02**, still `5dd898f8` — no change"*.
**Root cause:** I checked P1 (banner ↔ queue head), both halves agreed, and I stopped. The STATE row
is a THIRD copy of the same fact and nothing in my check looked at it.
**‼ THIS IS NOT A NEW LESSON. CLAUDE.md ALREADY SAYS IT, VERBATIM:** *"A CHECKLIST PROTECTS EXACTLY
WHAT IT ENUMERATES — when a fact lives in THREE places, updating the two that are named is the most
dangerous state of all, because the pair check then returns PASS."* I reproduced the documented
defect **inside the commit whose entire purpose was to leave the tree safe for a cold start**, and
on the exact subject of the first action I had just written.
**Fix:** the row now carries the moved state, the tree-hash verification, the one-file diff, and an
explicit note that it is the third home of this fact and must move with the other two.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔⛔ **BEFORE CLAIMING A PAIR CHECK PASSED, `grep` THE FILE FOR THE FACT ITSELF
— not for the two locations you already know about.** For a date or a commit hash that is literally
`grep -n "5dd898f8" 04-HANDOFF.md`, which takes one second and would have found this. ⭐ The general
form: **P1–P5 name LOCATIONS, but staleness attaches to FACTS.** Enumerate the fact's homes by
searching, then check the pairs.

### 2. ⛔ THE STATE TABLE COMMANDED WORK THAT HAD SHIPPED THE DAY BEFORE
**Symptom:** the §Ch24 STATE row said *"the remaining gap is `ch24_chapter_done()` + the `_play`
dispatch + the retargeted END-OF-CONTENT banner, which MUST land together"*. All three landed
2026-09-25 (`pokemon_league.py:3499`, `story_mode.py:5287`/`:5306`/`:5314`, banner `:5316-5325`).
**Root cause:** the previous session updated the banner, the queue and the punch list — P1 and P5 —
and not the STATE table, which is a fourth home for the same claim.
**Why it is the expensive kind:** the STATE table is what a cold agent reads to answer *"what is
left?"*. The Tier 2 auditor read it exactly that way and reported it as an instruction.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **THE STATE TABLE IS A CLAIM ABOUT WHAT REMAINS, SO IT IS A PAIR-HALF FOR
EVERY SHIPPED ITEM.** When an item ships, `grep` the STATE table for its symbols before saying the
docs are updated.

### 3. ⛔ A SPLICE DUPLICATED A SENTENCE VERBATIM, CONSECUTIVELY
**Symptom:** the queue head contained *"✅⭐ **JUST SHIPPED, DO NOT REBUILD: the PC-FIRST HM PATH IS
DRIVEN** (`#24-hm-slaves`, the WITHDRAW half)."* **twice in a row.**
**Root cause:** I anchored on the queue head's opening and re-emitted the following sentence as part
of my replacement, while the original copy was still there. The anchor assert passed — it was
unique — and asserted nothing about what followed it.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **AN ANCHOR ASSERT PROVES THE MATCH IS UNIQUE, NEVER THAT THE RESULT READS
CORRECTLY.** When a splice re-emits ANY text that already exists after the anchor, re-read the
spliced line. On a 14,000-character line that means grepping it for the re-emitted sentence and
counting — `grep -o "<sentence>" | wc -l` must return 1.

### 4. ⛔⛔ THE DOCS SENT A COLD AGENT TO RUN A MERGE ONTO `main` WITHOUT SAYING SO
**Symptom:** the first action said *"run the 5-step procedure"*, of which step 2 is
`git subtree pull --prefix=... --squash`. **Neither cold-start file said that this fetches AND
MERGES onto `main`**, that force-push is banned here so it is not trivially undoable once pushed,
that CLAUDE.md requires asking the user before a git operation of that shape, or that
`git subtree pull` runs `ensure_clean()` and dies `fatal: working tree has modifications` on a dirty
tree. Only a THIRD file (`40cakes repo/UPDATE-LOG.md`) mentioned the merge.
**Why this is the most serious of the four:** the other three misdescribe state; this one would have
caused an unapproved, hard-to-undo write to `main`. ‼ And the audit found the tree was dirty at that
moment, so the printed command would have died anyway — the instruction was both unsafe and
unrunnable.
**Fix:** the safety gate is stated **at the point of instruction** — ask the user first, take the
restore point, require a clean tree — plus the two facts the docs withheld (the snapshot dir is
dated for the OUTGOING commit, `2026-07-17-5dd898f8`; the upstream diff is one file,
`modules/gui/__init__.py` ⇒ `04-interfaces-gui-web-streaming.md`).
**Prevention rule:** ⛔⛔ **A SAFETY CONSTRAINT MUST LIVE WHERE THE ACTION IS COMMANDED, NOT IN THE
FILE THAT EXPLAINS THE PROCEDURE.** A cold agent reads the instruction and runs it; a warning one
pointer away is a warning that arrives after the merge commit exists. ⭐ And when an instruction's
first step is a git write to a shared branch, the instruction itself must name the approval gate.

### 5. ⛔⛔ I FIXED #4 BY PUTTING THE SAFETY CAVEAT IN **1 OF 4 PLACES** — #1's RULE, RECURRING WITHIN THE HOUR
**Symptom:** the Tier 2 re-run PASSED and then reported that the *"this is a MERGE onto `main`, ASK
THE USER"* caveat existed only in the queue head, while the SAME imperative was issued caveat-free
in three other spots: the banner (*"Run the 5 steps"* — the first thing read), the if-stopped cell
(*"so no reconciliation is needed — **just run the 5 steps**"*, which actively DOWNPLAYS it), and
`40cakes repo/UPDATE-LOG.md`'s step 2 itself — the procedure all three pointers resolve to — a bare
`git subtree pull --squash` with no approval note.
**Root cause:** mistake #1 in this same entry, with a SAFETY RULE as the payload instead of a commit
hash. I had written its prevention rule (*"grep for the FACT, not the locations"*) minutes earlier
and did not apply it, because I did not think of an INSTRUCTION as a "fact" with multiple homes.
**‼ AND THE GREP I EVENTUALLY RAN UNDER-COUNTED:** `grep -c "5 steps"` returned 2, not 3, because
the queue head says *"5-**step** procedure"*. Only `grep -n "5 steps\|5-step\|subtree pull"` found
all of them.
**Fix:** all four homes now carry it, and in `UPDATE-LOG.md` it sits DIRECTLY UNDER the command.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔⛔ **AN INSTRUCTION IS A FACT WITH HOMES, AND A SAFETY CAVEAT MUST LIVE IN
EVERY ONE OF THEM.** A caveat in 1 of 4 places is not a partial safeguard — it is a safeguard that
fails for any reader who enters by one of the other three doors. ⭐ And when you grep for an
instruction, **grep for two or three PHRASINGS, never one**: prose paraphrases itself ("5 steps" vs
"5-step procedure") and a single-phrasing grep reports a clean result over the copies it missed.

### 6. ⛔ I WROTE A HARDCODED LINE COUNT INTO THE FILE THAT EXPLICITLY FORBIDS IT
**Symptom:** I added *"This file is at **900/900** lines (R3 goes RED at 901)"* to `04-HANDOFF.md`,
whose own `:142` reads *"⛔ **NO COUNT *AND NO LIMIT* IS QUOTED HERE ON PURPOSE**"* and whose `:432`
records a Tier 1 reviewer catching this very anti-pattern: *"A LINE-COUNT WRITTEN INTO THE FILE IT
COUNTS IS STALE THE MOMENT IT IS WRITTEN."*
**Root cause:** I was trying to warn a cold agent that there is no headroom — a real and useful
warning — and reached for the number instead of the tool.
**Fix:** *"little or no line headroom — run `lint_docs.py` for the real figure"*, plus a note that a
number was briefly quoted and why that is wrong.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **WHEN THE USEFUL WARNING IS "THIS IS NEAR A LIMIT", NAME THE TOOL, NEVER
THE NUMBER.** A measured value copied into prose is a citation that rots on the next edit; the
measurement command stays true forever.

### 7. ⛔ MY CITATION LANDED ON A COMMENT BLOCK ~55 LINES FROM THE THING IT NAMED
**Symptom:** I cited the retargeted end-of-content banner as `story_mode.py:5316-5325`. VERIFIED:
that range is a `#` comment *about* the retargeting. The banner is `context.message = (` at
**`:5378-5384`**.
**Root cause:** I grepped for the retargeting text, found the comment that explains it first, and
cited the hit without checking it was the CODE rather than the commentary about the code.
**Fix:** the repair now cites **symbols** (`ch24_chapter_done`, the `_play` dispatch, the `_guard`,
the `context.message` banner) and names the **fork** — these exist only in `sandbox-pokebot/`, and
`custom-pokebot/story_mode.py:5287` is something else entirely.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **A GREP HIT ON DESCRIPTIVE TEXT IS USUALLY THE COMMENT, NOT THE CODE — the
comment is where the words live.** Cite the SYMBOL (the file's own standing rule), and when a repo
has two forks of the same file, **name the fork or the citation is ambiguous by construction.**


## 2026-09-26 — THE ENDLESS BATCH'S "RUN LENGTH" WAS *THIS END MINUS THE LAST END* FOR TWO MONTHS — and the gate that guarded it was never in the suite

**Symptom:** the 2026-09-15 endless corpus logs `derailed: Ch23 (Victory Road) failed ... (187,804
frames)`. A NEW GAME cannot reach §Ch23 in 188k frames.
**Root cause:** `StoryEndlessResetMode.run()` reads `start_frame` BEFORE `super().run()` hard-resets
the emulator, and `get_frame_count()` restarts on reset. So from run 2 on, `now - start_frame` was
"this run's end minus the previous session's end". The 2026-07-26 fix saw only the NEGATIVE half
(`finished (-959,198 frames)`), CLAMPED it to 0 and printed a warning — the positive-but-wrong half
printed silently. ‼ **And the budget wrapper right above had already solved the identical problem**
(re-base to 0 when the counter goes backwards): two code paths measured one quantity two ways, and
only the ENFORCED one was right.
**Second defect, same file:** `repro_endless_frame_budget.py` has existed since 2026-07-27 and was
**never registered in `run_gates.py`** — so it protected nothing for two months.
**Fix:** the outcome line reports the wrapper's own enforced, re-based count (`_run_elapsed_frames`);
the gate was extended (with a fault arm) and registered. See `07-CHANGELOG.md` 2026-09-26.
**Prevention rules:**
* ⛔ **WHEN TWO CODE PATHS MEASURE THE SAME QUANTITY, THE REPORTED VALUE MUST BE DERIVED FROM THE
  ENFORCED ONE** — never recompute it separately.
* ⛔ **A CLAMP HIDES THE HALF OF A BUG YOU COULD NOT SEE.** When a value can go impossible (negative),
  ask why before clamping — the same cause usually produces plausible-looking wrong values too.
* ⛔ **A REPRO IS NOT A GATE UNTIL `run_gates.py` NAMES IT.** Before writing "gated", `grep` the
  filename in `run_gates.py`.


## 2026-09-26 — A NAVIGATION TARGET CHOSEN INSIDE A TRAINER'S PATROL, FROM ONE INSTANT'S "IT'S FREE" (`#26-carleestage`)

**Symptom:** 9 of 39 badge-8 organic runs died at `Could not reach (101, 26) on ROUTE128 … still at (101, 25)`.
**Root cause:** on 2026-09-03 `CHANNEL_STAGE = (101,26)` was chosen because `calculate_path` returned a
path to it (32 wp) — a reading taken at ONE instant. The tile lies inside Carlee's patrol (x=101, y26-32)
and is exactly where she stops when she walks up to a bot at (101,25). ‼ **The code already knew half of
this:** the same function's comment says `_navigate_riding_out`'s fail-fast "assumes nothing can differ
between attempts, which is false against a WALKING NPC" — and then aimed it at a tile a walking NPC can
occupy permanently.
**Fix:** accept the adjacent tile when (and only when) a live object stands on the stage; A/B-proven with
a 48-offset sweep (`#26-carleestage`, `07-CHANGELOG.md` 2026-09-26).
**Prevention rules:**
* ⛔ **A TILE MEASURED FREE IS FREE AT ONE INSTANT.** Before hardcoding a navigation target, check it
  against every NPC's MOVEMENT RANGE (`movement_range_x/y` in the map's object events) and against the
  tile a trainer STOPS ON when it approaches (the tile adjacent to the player along its sight line). If the
  target can be occupied, the arrival check must tolerate an occupant, or the target must move.
* ⛔ **A RARE ORGANIC FAILURE IS REPRODUCIBLE BY SWEEPING TIMING, NOT BY WAITING FOR IT.** One fixture
  replayed over idle offsets reproduced the death on 6 of 48 trajectories in minutes. The 2026-09-03 drive
  that proved leg 4 ran that fixture with NO offset — on today's code, offset 0 is one of the 42 that never
  meet it (an inference about 09-03's code, which has changed since, but the lesson does not depend on it).


## 2026-09-26 — A DETECTOR WHOSE SELF-TEST FED IT A STRING NO LOG CAN CONTAIN (`analyze_endless_batch.py`)

**Symptom:** the endless analyzer's "did ANY run enter a League interior?" falsification arm could never fire,
and its `--self-test` passed anyway. Its "none" was quoted in `07-CHANGELOG.md` as evidence.
**Root cause:** the arm matched names like `POKEMON LEAGUE` / `HALL OF FAME`, but the logger prints the
REGION-MAP SECTION name, and every League room is `MAPSEC_EVER_GRANDE_CITY` ⇒ `EVER GRANDE CITY(16,N)`. The
self-test checked the synthetic string `"EVER GRANDE CITY POKEMON LEAGUE"` — which no log line contains — so the
test verified the matcher against its own assumption, not against the instrument's real output.
**Fix:** name AND (group, number), ≥2 sightings; the self-test now pushes REAL captured line shapes (and real
decoys: the Poké Center, a mid-warp mis-read) through the SAME parser the report uses.
**Prevention rule:** ⛔ **A SELF-TEST MUST FEED THE DETECTOR A LINE COPIED FROM A REAL LOG, THROUGH THE SAME
PARSER THE REPORT USES.** A hand-typed "example" encodes the author's belief about the format, which is exactly
the thing under test. Grep the corpus for the shape first, then paste it.
